title: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
content_c:
Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
- Published
A ceasefire that began with the aim of getting food and medicine to the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky has been extended across the wider southern region of Kherson, according to sources.
Several thousand residents are trapped in the city with no access to food, water and electricity. On one side is the Dnipro river, while Russian forces are on the other and all the roads out are too dangerous.
However, no breaches of the truce that began early on Tuesday have so far been reported.
US First Lady Melania Trump, who helped broker the ceasefire along with Pope Leo XIV, said on Tuesday that the area involved had been expanded to provide "safe passage" for humanitarian convoys.
That was later corroborated by the press secretary to Ukraine's public ombudsman, and by Oleksandr Tolokonnikov, deputy head of Kherson, who said Russian shelling had stopped both in Kherson city, which is in Ukrainian hands, and the wider region.
Under the deal, the ceasefire will be followed by deliveries of humanitarian aid to Oleshky and then evacuations, planned for Friday, for anyone wishing to leave.
An estimated 1,700 to 2,000 people remain in Oleshky itself and a few thousand more in surrounding areas.
Many residents have resorted to cooking garden weeds to survive, telling the BBC they are suffering extreme hunger and want to leave.
Both sides said the ceasefire was being observed. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said everything was proceeding "according to plan", and paid tribute to US mediation and in particular representatives of Melania Trump.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said if the ceasefire produced results, it could "pave the way for other steps in the peace process".
A key official in President Volodymyr Zelensky's parliamentary party, David Arakhamia, said it would continue until 22:59 Ukrainian time on Sunday 1 November, and described the truce as the "largest de-escalation since 2022".
Before the war Oleshky was home to 24,000 people, but it was seized by Russia during the first days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022.
No shops are open, and the city has had no electricity, gas or water since the Kakhovka Dam was blown up in 2023, flooding the area and killing many people in Oleshky itself.
Conditions have become so desperate that not only is getting supplies into the city extremely difficult, but escaping is too risky because the routes out of Oleshky have been mined and subject to drone attack.
One woman told the BBC she had stepped on a landmine and was currently in hospital where she had undergone two operations: "I don't know how long I will have to spend there," she said, worried about not being able to join the evacuation.
Pope Leo appealed earlier this month to Russia's President Vladimir Putin to allow food and medical aid into Oleshky as well as a safe evacuation, and urged his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky to co-operate with Moscow over a ceasefire.
Then the White House said last week that Melania Trump had secured a ceasefire.
On Tuesday, the US first lady said on X that the area covered by the ceasefire "has expanded beyond Oleshky, within the Kherson region, to provide safe passage for the humanitarian convoys".
The current truce is supposed to enable roads to be cleared of mines for supplies to get into the city possibly on Thursday, and for residents to have safe passage out in an evacuation planned for Friday.
Russia's defence ministry said units from the army's Dnepr group had been conducting "engineering reconnaissance" and clearing main access roads into the village of "explosive and booby-trap devices".
Many details on the evacuation plans are unclear, and residents are wary of trusting officials with their names and addresses. However, a local volunteer told the BBC that about 500 people had already expressed interest by Tuesday afternoon.
Vladimir Saldo, the Russian-installed head of occupied areas of Kherson, said temporary accommodation had been prepared in the region itself as well as Russian-annexed Crimea and across the Russian border in the Rostov, Krasnodar and Stavropol regions.
Saldo told Russian media that most Oleshky residents wanted to leave the city and stay in Russia, although his account has not been corroborated on the ground.
It is hard to make contact with people there as communication is patchy and many are reluctant to speak of the situation in fear of reprisals from the Russians.
Those residents or relatives who have spoken to the BBC have expressed fears that Russia may not allow them to return to Ukraine, or might examine their phones and online activity for signs of Ukrainian support, which could put them in danger.
Ukraine's military general staff urged people not to trust unverified reports or spread rumours about "the routes, time and place of the movement of people and humanitarian convoys".
- Eating garden weeds to survive in Russian-occupied city cut off from food and water 
  - Published24 September
Zelensky has warned that routes out of Oleshky that are demined by Russia will ensure that those civilians leaving Oleshky will "head towards Russia and stay there".
He said some residents would get to Ukrainian-controlled territory "one way or another", and that ideally anyone trapped would be able to reach their destination and evacuate to Ukraine.
One resident called Serhii, who fled Oleshky through minefields around three weeks ago, said he had eventually returned to Ukraine via Russia and Belarus. He called for a route across the River Dnipro that avoided Russian-occupied territory, saying "you simply cannot trust the Russian Federation".
However, bridges across the River Dnipro have been destroyed and sources say the riverbank is also mined and dangerous, so crossing into Ukrainian-controlled territory appears impossible.
Across the river, in Kherson city, no explosions have been heard and no drone-related injuries reported since 03:00 (01:00 GMT) on Tuesday and cars and pedestrians have been moving freely, according to local reports.
"Judging from the fact that more people are walking around, it feels a bit calmer," Galina Kyrychenko, a resident in the city, told public broadcaster Suspilne.
Additional reporting by Anastasiia Levchenko in Kyiv.
description: The truce was originally planned for the stranded residents of Oleshky, and Russia and Ukraine say no breaches have been reported.

title: Minimum wage set to rise but 18-20 year-olds will not get bigger increase
content_c:
Minimum wage set to rise but 18-20 year-olds will not get bigger increase
- Published
The rise in the minimum wage is expected to be announced in the Budget, but 18-to-20 year-olds are set to see lower increases than in previous years, the BBC understands.
Pay for younger workers will rise in line with the increase in minimum pay for employees aged 21 years and over.
However, the increase for younger workers is lower than that seen in the previous two years, when Labour raised the rate to meet a manifesto promise that it would remove "discriminatory age bands" with all adults entitled to the same minimum wage.
Chancellor John Healey is also announcing measures to give families what he is calling "breathing space" with the cost of living.
"The manifesto pledge on equalisation still applies but we were always clear it could happen over time," Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds told the BBC:
"Of course, you want not just good wages but good work, " he added. "It is a balance of making sure the pressures on the labour market are taken into account."
The Times reported that the National Minimum Wage for 18-to-20 year-olds is likely to rise by 3.9% from £10.85 an hour to around £11.27.
That is a smaller rise than the 26% increase the Labour government has put in place for younger workers since returning to power in 2024.
Even after the reported rise, the rate remains below the National Living Wage for older workers, which is currently £12.71 an hour. It is set to rise by 3.9% to £13.20, the Times said.
Andrea Egan, general secretary of the union Unison, said it was "deeply unfair" to keep paying different rates for the same job.
"Twenty year-old care workers, teaching assistants and security guards do the same work as their older colleagues," she said. "They don't pay less in the supermarket or at the petrol pump. They must be paid equally."
'Not going to change the world'
The government has also announced a number of measures, including removing import taxes on some food and ending the so-called cliff-edge for those receiving carer's allowance payments.
It says removing tariffs from 100 food items could save households up to £21 per year - or 40p a week - when combined with existing tariff suspensions that were introduced in June.
"We're not going to say it is everything," Reynolds told the BBC, but taken alongside the changes implemented in the summer on goods such as pasta, fruit juice and tuna, he said it would save around £500m a year.
Other measures the government announced on Tuesday included:
- Making permanent a 55p per mile tax-free mileage rate for those driving up to 10,000 miles for work, with the rate rising from 25p per mile to 35p above that
- Allowing carers to earn more than an existing earnings limit without losing their entire allowance, replacing it with a taper mechanism instead. However, this will not come in until 2030
- Giving two weeks of paternity pay to self-employed fathers, who have previously missed out on payments of up to £194 a week for the period
- And rolling out hundreds of additional Post Office drop boxes to make sending parcels easier
Speaking to the BBC's Newscast, Healey said: "None of this is going to change the world. But if it helps around the margins and its action the government can take, then I want try and fix it."
The government will also freeze fuel duty again in the Budget, the BBC understands. The 5p duty discount is also set to continue. That discount was first introduced in 2022, and was due to last 12 months, but has been extended ever since.
- What is the Budget and what could be in it? 
  - Published5 hours ago
The list of products the government is removing tariffs on includes:
- Baked beans
- Garlic
- Gherkins
- Chocolate-coated wafers and waffles
- Boiled sweets
- Toffees, caramels and similar sweets
- Citrus jams, marmalades and pastes
- Throat pastilles and cough drops
- Plant-based drinks including soya, nut, cereal or seed
- Kerosene
- Fertilisers
The government said removing tariffs on fertiliser aimed to help farmers, while changes to import levies on kerosene is targeted at households that rely on heating oil.
The Treasury said it would publish on Wednesday a full list of the products that will have tariffs removed.
A tariff is an import duty paid by domestic businesses buying products from overseas.
Asked why the government was making it cheaper to buy goods from abroad rather than cutting business costs for UK firms, Reynolds said: "Where you can make a reduction in the cost of importing goods into the UK, when you think you can balance that with your domestic economic interests, that's a decision we will take."
But Balwinder Dhoot, director of sustainability and growth at the Food and Drink Federation (FDF), said: "It's more expensive to make food and drink here in the UK than in many of our close neighbours, as businesses face such high energy costs."
The Conservatives said the government's "everyday fixes" had already been wiped out by higher borrowing costs, taxes and inflation.
Shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith said: "Shoppers face rising costs at the till and families are struggling to make ends meet, but Burnham's plan is cheaper gherkins. This is an insult to families hammered by Labour's tax rises."

content:
Minimum wage set to rise but 18-20 year-olds will not get bigger increase
- Published
The rise in the minimum wage is expected to be announced in the Budget, but 18-to-20 year-olds are set to see lower increases than in previous years, the BBC understands.
Pay for younger workers will rise in line with the increase in minimum pay for employees aged 21 years and over.
However, the increase for younger workers is lower than that seen in the previous two years, when Labour raised the rate to meet a manifesto promise that it would remove "discriminatory age bands" with all adults entitled to the same minimum wage.
Chancellor John Healey is also announcing measures to give families what he is calling "breathing space" with the cost of living.
"The manifesto pledge on equalisation still applies but we were always clear it could happen over time," Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds told the BBC:
"Of course, you want not just good wages but good work, " he added. "It is a balance of making sure the pressures on the labour market are taken into account."
The Times reported that the National Minimum Wage for 18-to-20 year-olds is likely to rise by 3.9% from £10.85 an hour to around £11.27.
That is a smaller rise than the 26% increase the Labour government has put in place for younger workers since returning to power in 2024.
Even after the reported rise, the rate remains below the National Living Wage for older workers, which is currently £12.71 an hour. It is set to rise by 3.9% to £13.20, the Times said.
Andrea Egan, general secretary of the union Unison, said it was "deeply unfair" to keep paying different rates for the same job.
"Twenty year-old care workers, teaching assistants and security guards do the same work as their older colleagues," she said. "They don't pay less in the supermarket or at the petrol pump. They must be paid equally."
'Not going to change the world'
The government has also announced a number of measures, including removing import taxes on some food and ending the so-called cliff-edge for those receiving carer's allowance payments.
It says removing tariffs from 100 food items could save households up to £21 per year - or 40p a week - when combined with existing tariff suspensions that were introduced in June.
"We're not going to say it is everything," Reynolds told the BBC, but taken alongside the changes implemented in the summer on goods such as pasta, fruit juice and tuna, he said it would save around £500m a year.
Other measures the government announced on Tuesday included:
- Making permanent a 55p per mile tax-free mileage rate for those driving up to 10,000 miles for work, with the rate rising from 25p per mile to 35p above that
- Allowing carers to earn more than an existing earnings limit without losing their entire allowance, replacing it with a taper mechanism instead. However, this will not come in until 2030
- Giving two weeks of paternity pay to self-employed fathers, who have previously missed out on payments of up to £194 a week for the period
- And rolling out hundreds of additional Post Office drop boxes to make sending parcels easier
Speaking to the BBC's Newscast, Healey said: "None of this is going to change the world. But if it helps around the margins and its action the government can take, then I want try and fix it."
The government will also freeze fuel duty again in the Budget, the BBC understands. The 5p duty discount is also set to continue. That discount was first introduced in 2022, and was due to last 12 months, but has been extended ever since.

title: Luxury cruise passengers stranded in Cambodia due to soaring fuel costs
content_c:
Luxury cruise passengers stranded in Cambodia due to soaring fuel costs
- Published
A luxury cruise ship on a years-long voyage around the world said it suspended operations due to extraordinarily high fuel costs, leaving passengers stranded in Cambodia.
The US-based operator of Villa Vie Odyssey said it was working with passengers on disembarkation plans and "temporary living arrangements".
It is unclear how many were on board but the nearly 200m (656ft) vessel can carry up to 650 passengers. It departed Belfast in October 2024 for a "continuous voyage around the world".
Global fuel prices have soared since the Iran war started earlier this year. The ship's operator said the monthly fuel cost per cabin in parts of Asia has risen to as much as $8,000 (£6,000) from $1,800.
The company said it had taken "significant steps to reduce fuel consumption, including slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port". But those measures turned out to be insufficient to "offset the extraordinary increase in fuel costs".
"Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution," it said.
The company would spend the next 60 days on "restructuring and recapitalisation", though "no outcome is assured", it said.
The Villa Vie Odyssey's voyage was expected to span 3.5 years and cover nearly 150 countries, according to its website.
Its departure had faced delays as the ship underwent repairs, leaving passengers stranded in Belfast for months and costing the company millions of pounds.
The ship was more than 750 days into its circumnavigation before announcing its suspension of its journey on Tuesday - which means its passengers would now be stranded in Cambodia.
There were around 200 passengers on board when they were ordered to disembark in Cambodia, Bloomberg reported, citing the cruise operator's founder.
The Villa Vie Odyssey is equipped with several bars and restaurants, a pool deck and a pickleball court, according to its website.
Permanent residencies in its cabins range from $120,000 to $440,000. These cabins are also also available for rent from $3,500 a month.
Last year, the company launched a lifetime residence programme for people to spend their retirement years at sea.
In 2024, days after US President Donald Trump won his second term, Villa Vie Residences announced a four-year "Skip Forward" package. Its CEO told Fox Business at the time that it was the "perfect product for those who said they'd leave the country if 'XYZ' wins the election".

title: Trump shows off tanker with ‘1m barrels of oil’ and floats Venezuela as 51st state
content_c:
Donald Trump suggested Venezuela would become the 51st state of the United States on Tuesday as the president showed off a tanker he claimed had “one million barrels of oil on it” from the country, nine months after deposing its president.
At a campaign rally in Corpus Christ, Texas, Trump touted a US oil deal with Venezuela, which the US attacked in January, capturing its long-serving leader Nicolás Maduro.
Trump claims the agreement – struck with the South American country’s interim government, which is backed by Trump’s administration – will cover “billions” of barrels of oil.
Venezuela “will become a prosperous country, and who knows? Maybe some day soon it’ll become a prosperous 51st state,” Trump said at the podium on Tuesday. “That’s possible.”
Venezuela is on a growing list of countries and territories Trump has spoken of acquiring, including Greenland, Canada and Mexico.
With tens of millions of Americans set to vote in next week’s midterm elections, Trump’s aggressive foreign policy – including his controversial war on Iran, and tariffs on goods from much of the world – have challenged his popularity, according to opinion polls, with his approval ratings falling to record lows.
But on Tuesday, the president sought to point to the Venezuela operation as an example of his success. US fuel prices, which surged after the start of the Iran war, piling pressure on Americans’ cost of living, “will soon come plummeting down”, he claimed in a social media post.
“We’re celebrating the greatest oil victory in history,” he said at the rally, pointing out the ship off the Texan coast. “The oil provided is being provided to the United States at zero cost to the American taxpayer.”
Moments before Trump took the stage in Texas, he claimed on his Truth Social platform: “By unleashing Energy Dominance from Alaska, all the way down to Venezuela, I have made the Western Hemisphere the Energy Capital of the World.”
The deal has also drawn skepticism as critics complained that the Trump administration has not pushed a transition to democracy in Venezuela, where elections have not been held since Maduro was detained by US forces and taken to New York to face criminal charges after a raid on his Caracas residence.
The urgency of the oil agreement stems from Trump’s opting into the war with Iran in February. Gas prices have shot up nationwide after Iran closed the strait of Hormuz, a passageway for 20% of the world’s oil supplies.

title: Homes across UK to get low- or no-interest loans to fund solar panels and heat pumps
content_c:
Households across the UK can now cut their energy bills by hundreds of pounds a year at no upfront cost by applying for interest-free or “low-interest” loans to fund upgrades such as heat pumps, batteries and solar panels.
The government-backed Warm Home Loans scheme, which launched on Tuesday, could mean thousands more households are able to access low-carbon energy alternative technologies, thanks to loans ranging from £7,500 to up £35,000.
Energy suppliers including British Gas and E.On have partnered with lenders from Tandem Bank and Homeserve respectively to offer the loans directly to customers at a discounted rate compared with those offered by high street lenders.
People interested in swapping their gas boiler for an air-source or ground-source heat pump could secure loans of up to £10,000 or £35,000 respectively, while also drawing on the government’s existing scheme which offers grants of up to £9,000 a year for households installing the replacements for fossil fuel heating.
Installing a heat pump, battery and solar panels could save households up to £550 a year on their energy bills, rising by a further £300 a year with a time-of-use tariff, according to the government.
Soaring energy costs have led to record demand for low-carbon home energy upgrades over the last year, and the government believes the loan scheme means “thousands more households” will be able to cut their energy bills by fitting clean energy technology and spreading repayments over many years.
Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, said: “Energy is an everyday essential that must be affordable for everyone. These government-supported loans will help families across the UK upgrade their homes with no upfront costs to make them warmer and cheaper to run.”
Chris Norbury, the chief executive of E.On UK, said that a recent trial showed that fuel-poor customers in Coventry were able to save more than £250 a year on average by combining a home battery with a time of use tariff that charges lower rates for using energy outside peak demand hours.
He said the Warm Homes Loan scheme was “an opportunity to take that further” by “removing barriers to low-carbon technologies”.
The government set out the terms of the new scheme a day before the chancellor, John Healey, delivers his first budget on Wednesday, which reportedly will include plans to scale back heat pump grants made through its boiler upgrade scheme.
The scheme is not expected to be scrapped altogether, but sources say hundreds of millions of pounds will be cut from its £2.7bn five-year budget because Treasury officials consider it a subsidy used mainly by middle-class households.
It has typically provided grants of up to £7,500 to help meet the £13,600 cost of installing a heat pump, meaning households have still required a significant outlay to make up the difference.
The Guardian understands that grants of up to £9,000 a year are likely to remain available to households that are not connected to the gas grid and are forced to rely on high-cost heating oil. These grants could be used alongside the low-interest loans to cover the full cost of a heat pump.
Other lenders taking part in the Warm Home Loans scheme include HTG Finance, Propensio, Secure Trust Bank, Selina Finance, South Manchester Credit Union, Sunsave, The Money Co-op and This Bank.

title: Israel election: Exit polls show no clear winner, with Netanyahu's fate unclear
content_c:
Israel election: Exit polls show no clear winner
Published October 27, 2026last updated October 28, 2026
What you need to know
- Israelis have voted, at a high turnout, in a parliamentary election that appears to have produced no clear winner
- The pro-Netanyahu bloc and anti-Netanyahu bloc each have 51 seats, according to public broadcaster KAN
- Two Arab parties have gained 18 seats between them
- At least 61 seats are needed to form a secure majority
- Israel election committee reports highest voter turnout on record as of 2 p.m., halfway through the voting day
- Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, faces a staunch challenge to his grip on power
- His chief rival is former military chief Gadi Eisenkot
- Eisenkot called on Netanyahu to resign in post-election speech
- Netanyahu, meanwhile, called for a 'strong' right-wing government and said his Likud party is the biggest
Follow below for all the latest on the Israeli election on October 27, 2026, and its aftermath:
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add us as a Preferred Source on Google. Then tap the "Star" or "Preferred" to keep DW News at the top of your feed.
Netanyahu calls for 'strong' right-wing government after election
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to form a new right-wing government, despite exit polls showing no clear majority for either political bloc.
"We are still waiting for the real results," Netanyahu told cheering supporters in a speech early Wednesday, stressing that his Likud party was the largest in Israel.
"We must put in place a strong government of the right," he said.
Netanyahu also rejected the prospect of a government relying on the support of Arab parties, which made strong gains in Tuesday's election.
Turning to security, Netanyahu said Israel had a "unique opportunity" together with US President Donald Trump to end what he called the Iranian threat.
Updated exit polls show Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot either tied or separated by a narrow margin. Neither side is projected to win the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset.
Updated exit polls show Netanyahu and opposition blocs neck and neck
Updated Israeli exit polls suggest Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc is now tied with the opposition, after earlier projections showed a narrow lead for the bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot.
Public broadcaster Kan 11 and Channel 13 both put the pro-Netanyahu and anti-Netanyahu blocs at 51 seats each. Channel 12, meanwhile, is now showing the pro-Netanyahu camp with an edge at 52 seats and the opposition at 49 seats.
Kan 11's latest projection gives Netanyahu's Likud party 27 seats, up from 25 in its earlier poll.
However, none of the three major networks project either bloc winning the 61 seats needed for a majority in Israel's 120-seat parliament, the Knesset.
Eisenkot calls on Netanyahu to resign in post-election speech
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has called on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to step down, saying voters have sent a clear message that they want change.
"We've made history," Eisenkot told supporters in a speech in Jerusalem following Tuesday's election. "The public voted against the continuation of Netanyahu as prime minister."
He said a "decent leader" would accept the public's will and announce his resignation, warning that another round of elections would be a mistake.
Eisenkot pledged to work towards forming what he called a "Zionist conscription government," referring to his push for broader military service obligations.
"We would like to represent all Israelis," he said, adding that the country needed stable leadership and a government that represented all parts of society.
The former military chief also warned Netanyahu against making major security decisions or launching new wars, arguing that he no longer had a mandate to do so.
"Netanyahu: Don't you dare use Israel's security for your political needs," Eisenkot said.
Eisenkot says he is ready to form a government
Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the opposition bloc, said the election results pointed to a "complete lack of confidence" in Netanyahu and his coalition.
"I will act immediately to carry out the people’s mandate, replace Netanyahu's government and form a Zionist government committed to military conscription as soon as possible," Eisenkot said in a statement.
A former military chief, he made the issue of eliminating exemptions from military service for Ultra-Orthodox men central to his campaign.
Majority of Israeli public voted against Netanyahu, exit polls show
Much of the Israeli media labeled the Israeli election an opinion poll on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
If the exit polls of Israel's main news outlets are anything to go by, the Israeli public voted against the country's longest-serving prime minister.
While Netanyahu's current coalition includes 68 seats, the exit polls gave his bloc between 50 and 51 seats.
The Israeli prime minister is unlikely to concede defeat despite his coalition having taken a significant hit, but it remains to be seen how Likud's own ranks, as well as its coalition partners, will react to the exit polls.
Ra'am party becomes political power broker
The success of Ra'am, which exit polls predict will take seven seats, means no Israeli government can be established without the religious Muslim party playing some part.
The party already made headlines after appointing Yoav Segalovich, a Jewish former high-ranking police chief, as the number two candidate to leader Mansour Abbas. The raging criminality and violence across the Arab and Palestinian community, as well as the war in Gaza, both could have played a role in Ra'am's result.
Both the Likud-led coalition and large parts of the Israeli opposition may have ruled out a coalition with Ra'am, but the current results may leave them little choice but to seek some form of cooperation with the party.
As one Israeli pollster put it, "Tonight, Israelis were reminded that their population also includes Arabs and Palestinians with Israeli citizenship."
Netanyahu's bloc trails in Israel election, exit polls say
Exit polls from Israel's major television networks project that a majority of Israelis voted against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition, but his Likud party has emerged as the largest single group in the Knesset, with 25 projected seats.
Challenger Gadi Eisenkot's bloc has emerged as the largest group with a projected 53, just ahead of the ruling coalition on 50, but well short of the 61 needed for a majority.
Neither bloc has a clear majority without the support of Arab parties.
These projected numbers are from public broadcaster Kan 11; other numbers vary by channel, but only slightly.
Polls closing around the country
It's now 10 p.m. across Israel, which means that polling stations around the country either should have closed or should be making preparations to do so as the last people in line cast their ballots.
Exit polls should follow shortly on Israeli television. These have a fairly good reputation overall but of course are only projections.
Results will start to trickle in through the night and are unlikely to be finalized until Wednesday.
And of course, there's every chance that even once the dust has settled and the final results are in, we will have a longer wait until there's clarity about who might be able to form a coalition government.
In any case, stick with us and we'll keep you posted.
Election commission sees 'no need to extend voting hours' after Netanyahu request
The Central Elections Committee has rejected a request by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party and some other groups to extend voting beyond 10 p.m. (2000 UTC/GMT).
"High nationwide turnout across all sectors of society reflects strong public engagement in the democratic process, and no need to extend voting hours was identified," a commission statement said.
The committee noted, however, that this decision was based on the circumstances "as things stand," leaving open the possibility for matters to change.
For instance, voting hours have been extended in some areas, including a polling location used by Israeli settlers in Hebron, in the occupied West Bank, where a power outage led to an extension of the closing time from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. Polling stations with fewer than 350 eligible voters typically close two hours earlier than larger polling stations in urban areas.
The commission has also said several times that anybody who started queueing before closing time will be given a chance to vote.
IN DEPTH: How AI reshaped Israel's election campaign
Artificial intelligence is emerging as a major factor in Israel's election campaign, with political parties using AI-generated videos, automated calls and online content on a large scale.
DW's Josh Axelrod examined the growing role of AI in the campaign, as researchers and analysts raise concerns about misleading content, bots and deepfakes ahead of the vote.
High turnout could spell problems for Netanyahu's bloc
The expected high turnout means the number of votes needed to cross the 3.25% threshold to enter the Knesset, the Israeli parliament, is going to be higher, meaning smaller parties are at risk of not making it.
According to opinion polls from last week, the two parties that are on the threshold limit are Amcha Israel, a far-right party led by former military commander Ofer Winter, and the Reservists Party, which has not declared support for either main bloc.
Winter repeatedly said he intends to join a Netanyahu coalition, and a scenario in which his party doesn't make it to parliament puts Likud's chances of a future coalition at risk.
Either way, Israel's Central Elections Committee will have to make a decision on the matter within the hour.
Turnout reaches 2 in 3 voters by 6 p.m.
Voter turnout reached 66.7%, or roughly two in every three eligible voters, by 6 p.m. local time, according to an update from the Central Elections Committee.
This remains the highest partial turnout figure since such records were first taken in 1973.
The level is only slightly clear of the previous high of 65.2% in 1973 and 1988 — but it quite considerably surpasses the 57.7% who had voted by this time in 2022.
And that figure had already been the highest 6 p.m. turnout of the 21st century before being surpassed today.
WATCH: Could Arab voters hold the key in Israel’s election?
Arab voters could play a decisive role in Israel's election. With neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor Gadi Eisenkot expected to win a Knesset majority, Arab parties could become key to forming the next government.
Activists worked to boost voter turnout, especially among young voters.
Netanyahu emphasizes Arab turnout in appeals to his own voters
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu continued issuing appeals to supporters to go out and vote online as the day progressed.
One common theme was apparent in almost all of the posts: warnings about high turnout in Arab and to a lesser extent left-leaning communities.
"We're at war for our home," one of Netanyahu's posts read, using a phrase that appeared repeatedly in his messaging. "Muslim Brotherhood supporters are raiding the polling stations and stealing the elections. Go out and vote, recover it!!"
In another post he showed an image claiming to show a long line of voters queueing in Rahat, with a crowd of women wearing niqab coverings prominently visible at the front of the queue, suggesting that they were Muslim Palestinian voters.
Sami Abou Shahadeh, the leader of the Balad party, which is part of the alliance known as the Joint List, in turn called on his supporters to vote before the deadline expired, also highlighting similar appeals to voters from the leader of the far-right Jewish Power party, Itamar Ben-Gvir.
"There is one response to the incitement by Ben-Gvir and Netanyahu against the Arab citizens that has been going on all day: go out and vote for the Joint List!" he wrote.

"It would be good for Israel, if it were to come to a change, because I believe that [Prime Minister Benjamin] Netanyahu has squandered a great deal of trust in recent years, both in foreign and domestic policy," Beck said in an interview broadcast on sister channels RTL and ntv.

He also criticized domestic efforts by the Likud-led government to reform the legal system and its influence over politics, saying this would "fundamentally change Israel's character, and should be stopped."
Beck said he hoped that a functioning majority would emerge from the vote, but acknowledged that pollsters anticipated a stalemate. In that scenario, he said, he would personally favor a national unity government incorporating all the major players.
But at present he thought the "divide between the two camps is so deep, that it really would be a bit of a masterstroke to be able to bring them together." He made a similar comment online, saying such a unity govermment "would be good" but was "not very likely."
description: While partial results show the pro-Netanyahu and anti-Netanyahu blocs almost even, it may take days for the final tally. DW has the latest.

Israel election: Exit polls show no clear winner
Published October 27, 2026last updated October 28, 2026
What you need to know
- Israelis have voted, at a high turnout, in a parliamentary election that appears to have produced no clear winner
- The pro-Netanyahu bloc and anti-Netanyahu bloc each have 51 seats, according to public broadcaster KAN
- Two Arab parties have gained 18 seats between them
- At least 61 seats are needed to form a secure majority
- Israel election committee reports highest voter turnout on record as of 2 p.m., halfway through the voting day
- Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, faces a staunch challenge to his grip on power
- His chief rival is former military chief Gadi Eisenkot
- Eisenkot called on Netanyahu to resign in post-election speech
- Netanyahu, meanwhile, called for a 'strong' right-wing government and said his Likud party is the biggest
Follow below for all the latest on the Israeli election on October 27, 2026, and its aftermath:
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add us as a Preferred Source on Google. Then tap the "Star" or "Preferred" to keep DW News at the top of your feed.
Netanyahu calls for 'strong' right-wing government after election
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to form a new right-wing government, despite exit polls showing no clear majority for either political bloc.
"We are still waiting for the real results," Netanyahu told cheering supporters in a speech early Wednesday, stressing that his Likud party was the largest in Israel.
"We must put in place a strong government of the right," he said.
Netanyahu also rejected the prospect of a government relying on the support of Arab parties, which made strong gains in Tuesday's election.
Turning to security, Netanyahu said Israel had a "unique opportunity" together with US President Donald Trump to end what he called the Iranian threat.
Updated exit polls show Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot either tied or separated by a narrow margin. Neither side is projected to win the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset.
Updated exit polls show Netanyahu and opposition blocs neck and neck
Updated Israeli exit polls suggest Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc is now tied with the opposition, after earlier projections showed a narrow lead for the bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot.
Public broadcaster Kan 11 and Channel 13 both put the pro-Netanyahu and anti-Netanyahu blocs at 51 seats each. Channel 12, meanwhile, is now showing the pro-Netanyahu camp with an edge at 52 seats and the opposition at 49 seats.
Kan 11's latest projection gives Netanyahu's Likud party 27 seats, up from 25 in its earlier poll.
However, none of the three major networks project either bloc winning the 61 seats needed for a majority in Israel's 120-seat parliament, the Knesset.
Eisenkot calls on Netanyahu to resign in post-election speech
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has called on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to step down, saying voters have sent a clear message that they want change.
"We've made history," Eisenkot told supporters in a speech in Jerusalem following Tuesday's election. "The public voted against the continuation of Netanyahu as prime minister."
He said a "decent leader" would accept the public's will and announce his resignation, warning that another round of elections would be a mistake.
Eisenkot pledged to work towards forming what he called a "Zionist conscription government," referring to his push for broader military service obligations.
"We would like to represent all Israelis," he said, adding that the country needed stable leadership and a government that represented all parts of society.
The former military chief also warned Netanyahu against making major security decisions or launching new wars, arguing that he no longer had a mandate to do so.
"Netanyahu: Don't you dare use Israel's security for your political needs," Eisenkot said.
Eisenkot says he is ready to form a government
Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the opposition bloc, said the election results pointed to a "complete lack of confidence" in Netanyahu and his coalition.
"I will act immediately to carry out the people’s mandate, replace Netanyahu's government and form a Zionist government committed to military conscription as soon as possible," Eisenkot said in a statement.
A former military chief, he made the issue of eliminating exemptions from military service for Ultra-Orthodox men central to his campaign.
Majority of Israeli public voted against Netanyahu, exit polls show
Much of the Israeli media labeled the Israeli election an opinion poll on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
If the exit polls of Israel's main news outlets are anything to go by, the Israeli public voted against the country's longest-serving prime minister.
While Netanyahu's current coalition includes 68 seats, the exit polls gave his bloc between 50 and 51 seats.
The Israeli prime minister is unlikely to concede defeat despite his coalition having taken a significant hit, but it remains to be seen how Likud's own ranks, as well as its coalition partners, will react to the exit polls.
Ra'am party becomes political power broker
The success of Ra'am, which exit polls predict will take seven seats, means no Israeli government can be established without the religious Muslim party playing some part.
The party already made headlines after appointing Yoav Segalovich, a Jewish former high-ranking police chief, as the number two candidate to leader Mansour Abbas. The raging criminality and violence across the Arab and Palestinian community, as well as the war in Gaza, both could have played a role in Ra'am's result.
Both the Likud-led coalition and large parts of the Israeli opposition may have ruled out a coalition with Ra'am, but the current results may leave them little choice but to seek some form of cooperation with the party.
As one Israeli pollster put it, "Tonight, Israelis were reminded that their population also includes Arabs and Palestinians with Israeli citizenship."
Netanyahu's bloc trails in Israel election, exit polls say
Exit polls from Israel's major television networks project that a majority of Israelis voted against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition, but his Likud party has emerged as the largest single group in the Knesset, with 25 projected seats.
Challenger Gadi Eisenkot's bloc has emerged as the largest group with a projected 53, just ahead of the ruling coalition on 50, but well short of the 61 needed for a majority.
Neither bloc has a clear majority without the support of Arab parties.
These projected numbers are from public broadcaster Kan 11; other numbers vary by channel, but only slightly.
Polls closing around the country
It's now 10 p.m. across Israel, which means that polling stations around the country either should have closed or should be making preparations to do so as the last people in line cast their ballots.
Exit polls should follow shortly on Israeli television. These have a fairly good reputation overall but of course are only projections.
Results will start to trickle in through the night and are unlikely to be finalized until Wednesday.
And of course, there's every chance that even once the dust has settled and the final results are in, we will have a longer wait until there's clarity about who might be able to form a coalition government.
In any case, stick with us and we'll keep you posted.
Election commission sees 'no need to extend voting hours' after Netanyahu request
The Central Elections Committee has rejected a request by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party and some other groups to extend voting beyond 10 p.m. (2000 UTC/GMT).
"High nationwide turnout across all sectors of society reflects strong public engagement in the democratic process, and no need to extend voting hours was identified," a commission statement said.
The committee noted, however, that this decision was based on the circumstances "as things stand," leaving open the possibility for matters to change.
For instance, voting hours have been extended in some areas, including a polling location used by Israeli settlers in Hebron, in the occupied West Bank, where a power outage led to an extension of the closing time from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. Polling stations with fewer than 350 eligible voters typically close two hours earlier than larger polling stations in urban areas.
The commission has also said several times that anybody who started queueing before closing time will be given a chance to vote.
IN DEPTH: How AI reshaped Israel's election campaign
Artificial intelligence is emerging as a major factor in Israel's election campaign, with political parties using AI-generated videos, automated calls and online content on a large scale.
DW's Josh Axelrod examined the growing role of AI in the campaign, as researchers and analysts raise concerns about misleading content, bots and deepfakes ahead of the vote.
High turnout could spell problems for Netanyahu's bloc
The expected high turnout means the number of votes needed to cross the 3.25% threshold to enter the Knesset, the Israeli parliament, is going to be higher, meaning smaller parties are at risk of not making it.
According to opinion polls from last week, the two parties that are on the threshold limit are Amcha Israel, a far-right party led by former military commander Ofer Winter, and the Reservists Party, which has not declared support for either main bloc.
Winter repeatedly said he intends to join a Netanyahu coalition, and a scenario in which his party doesn't make it to parliament puts Likud's chances of a future coalition at risk.
Either way, Israel's Central Elections Committee will have to make a decision on the matter within the hour.
Turnout reaches 2 in 3 voters by 6 p.m.
Voter turnout reached 66.7%, or roughly two in every three eligible voters, by 6 p.m. local time, according to an update from the Central Elections Committee.
This remains the highest partial turnout figure since such records were first taken in 1973.
The level is only slightly clear of the previous high of 65.2% in 1973 and 1988 — but it quite considerably surpasses the 57.7% who had voted by this time in 2022.
And that figure had already been the highest 6 p.m. turnout of the 21st century before being surpassed today.

Arab voters could play a decisive role in Israel's election. With neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor Gadi Eisenkot expected to win a Knesset majority, Arab parties could become key to forming the next government.
Activists worked to boost voter turnout, especially among young voters.

title: Wo Deutschland noch wachsen kann: Zukunftsmärkte für heimische Firmen
content_c:
Zukunftsmärkte für Firmen Wo Deutschland noch wachsen kann
Die deutsche Wirtschaft hat viele Probleme. Doch bei all den negativen Nachrichten gibt es auch Chancen. Denn auf einigen Märkten der Zukunft haben heimische Unternehmen gute Karten.
Die deutsche Wirtschaft kommt seit Jahren kaum vom Fleck. Einstige Erfolgsgaranten schwächeln: die Automobilindustrie, der Maschinenbau, die Chemiebranche. Dazu wächst die Konkurrenz aus China, traditionelle Exportmärkte werden zunehmend schwieriger. Doch während vor allem über die Schwächen des Wirtschaftsstandorts Deutschland diskutiert wird, geraten die Chancen für neues Wachstum leicht aus dem Blick.
Insgesamt 14 dynamisch wachsende Märkte
Dabei ist Deutschland in manchen Zukunftsfeldern besser aufgestellt, als die Krisendebatte vermuten lässt. Die Unternehmensberatung McKinsey hat 14 dynamisch wachsende Märkte identifiziert, in denen deutsche Unternehmen gute Voraussetzungen mitbringen: von der Biotechnologie und Medizintechnik über Robotik und neue Werkstoffe bis hin zu klimafreundlichen Energietechnologien und Quantencomputing.
Das weltweite Marktpotenzial dieser "Wachstumsarenen" summiere sich bis 2040 auf mehr als 40 Billionen Dollar, sagt Luca Flora von McKinsey im Gespräch mit der ARD-Finanzredaktion.
Warum das Exportmodell an Grenzen stößt
Um diese Chancen zu nutzen, muss Deutschland nach Ansicht von Christian Rammer vom Leibniz-Zentrum für Europäische Wirtschaftsforschung (ZEW) auch sein bisheriges Erfolgsmodell überdenken: "Wir haben in den vergangenen Jahrzehnten Wachstum immer gedacht als Wachstum im Export: Wo können wir hier in Deutschland etwas herstellen und dann in die Welt verkaufen?"
Doch diese Strategie stößt zunehmend an ihre Grenzen - besonders deutlich zeigt sich das in der Autoindustrie. Angesichts wachsender Handelshemmnisse und geopolitischer Unsicherheiten hält Rammer es für wenig zukunftsfähig, Autos in Deutschland für den gesamten Weltmarkt zu produzieren. Die Hersteller verlagerten die Produktion zunehmend in die Nähe ihrer Absatzmärkte. Neue Wachstumschancen müsse Deutschland deshalb stärker im Inland und im europäischen Binnenmarkt suchen, so Rammer.
Dienstleistungen und Gesundheit als Wachstumsmärkte
Potenzial sieht der ZEW-Ökonom etwa dort, wo gesellschaftliche Herausforderungen neue Nachfrage schaffen: beim Wohnungsbau, im Gesundheitswesen und in der Pflege, bei der Anpassung an den Klimawandel sowie bei der Energie- und Wasserversorgung.
Deutschland konzentriere sich in der Wachstumsdebatte allerdings zu stark auf Fabriken und industrielle Produktion. Dabei eröffnet der Dienstleistungssektor nach seiner Einschätzung besonders große Möglichkeiten. "Wo Menschen für andere Menschen arbeiten - das ist eigentlich das große Wachstumsfeld", sagt Rammer.
Schon heute entstehen gut 71 Prozent der deutschen Bruttowertschöpfung im Dienstleistungssektor. Dennoch ist Deutschland im europäischen Vergleich weiterhin stark industriell geprägt: Auf das Produzierende Gewerbe entfielen 2025 hierzulande 22,9 Prozent der Bruttowertschöpfung, im EU-Durchschnitt waren es lediglich 19,1 Prozent.
Industrielle KI: Deutschlands besondere Stärke
Einige Fachleute sehen allerdings gerade in Deutschlands industrieller Tradition einen Vorteil. "Deutschland hat etwas, was dem Silicon Valley fehlt: nämlich Maschinen, Anlagen, Produktionsdaten - und das aus Jahrzehnten", sagt Barbara Engels, Expertin für nachhaltige Digitalisierung und Künstliche Intelligenz beim Institut der deutschen Wirtschaft (IW).
Deutsche Industrieunternehmen verfügten über einen Datenschatz, den es in dieser Form nirgendwo sonst auf der Welt gebe. "Made in Germany besteht meiner Ansicht nach auch im KI-Zeitalter fort", so Engels.
Chancen für den Mittelstand in der Robotik
Entscheidend ist es dabei, industrielle Erfahrung und Künstliche Intelligenz miteinander zu verbinden. In der sogenannten "physischen KI" kann besonders gut gelingen: Humanoide Roboter benötigen präzise Antriebe, Sensoren und komplexe Steuerungstechnik.
"Und genau solche Komponenten werden von deutschen Spezialisten, vielfach aus dem Mittelstand heraus, sehr erfolgreich in Deutschland entwickelt, hergestellt und vertrieben", sagt McKinsey-Experte Flora. "Das heißt, wir müssen als Deutschland gar nicht zwingend eine gesamte Wertschöpfungskette beherrschen, um trotzdem am Markt teilzuhaben."
Viel ungenutztes Potenzial bei den Firmen?
Dass KI deutschen Unternehmen auch jenseits der Robotik wirtschaftliche Chancen bietet, zeigt eine KfW-Untersuchung vom September. Mittelständische Unternehmen, die KI einsetzen, weisen demnach im Schnitt ein stärkeres Umsatzwachstum, eine höhere Produktivität und bessere Renditen auf.
Überhaupt scheinen viele Unternehmen hierzulande ihr Potenzial kaum auszuschöpfen. Das geht aus einer Analyse der Unternehmensberatung McKinsey hervor. Zwischen 2019 und 2023 waren gerade einmal 29 von 16.200 untersuchten Firmen - 0,2 Prozent - für 47 Prozent des Produktivitätswachstums in dieser Unternehmensgruppe verantwortlich. Dabei verlaufe die entscheidende Trennlinie nicht zwischen Branchen, betont McKinsey-Experte Jan Krause, sondern "zwischen Mut und Zögern".
Bürokratie bremst Investitionen
Ein Grund für die Zurückhaltung vieler Unternehmen ist nach Einschätzung von ZEW-Ökonom Christian Rammer die Bürokratie. Zu viele Vorschriften, langwierige Genehmigungsverfahren - all das bremse Investitionen, selbst wenn die Nachfrage vorhanden sei. Unternehmen liefen dadurch Gefahr, wichtige Marktchancen zu verpassen. Oder wie Rammer es formuliert: "Bis wir damit durch sind, ist vielleicht der Markt schon wieder weg oder andere waren einfach schneller."
An Wachstumschancen mangelt es Deutschland also nicht. Bleibt nur die Frage, wie sich die Voraussetzungen schaffen lassen, um sie auch zu nutzen.

Dennoch ist Deutschland im europäischen Vergleich weiterhin stark industriell geprägt: Auf das Produzierende Gewerbe entfielen 2025 hierzulande 22,9 Prozent der Bruttowertschöpfung, im EU-Durchschnitt waren es lediglich 19,1 Prozent.
Industrielle KI: Deutschlands besondere Stärke
Einige Fachleute sehen allerdings gerade in Deutschlands industrieller Tradition einen Vorteil. "Deutschland hat etwas, was dem Silicon Valley fehlt: nämlich Maschinen, Anlagen, Produktionsdaten - und das aus Jahrzehnten", sagt Barbara Engels, Expertin für nachhaltige Digitalisierung und Künstliche Intelligenz beim Institut der deutschen Wirtschaft (IW).
Deutsche Industrieunternehmen verfügten über einen Datenschatz, den es in dieser Form nirgendwo sonst auf der Welt gebe. "Made in Germany besteht meiner Ansicht nach auch im KI-Zeitalter fort", so Engels.
Chancen für den Mittelstand in der Robotik
Entscheidend ist es dabei, industrielle Erfahrung und Künstliche Intelligenz miteinander zu verbinden. In der sogenannten "physischen KI" kann besonders gut gelingen: Humanoide Roboter benötigen präzise Antriebe, Sensoren und komplexe Steuerungstechnik.
"Und genau solche Komponenten werden von deutschen Spezialisten, vielfach aus dem Mittelstand heraus, sehr erfolgreich in Deutschland entwickelt, hergestellt und vertrieben", sagt McKinsey-Experte Flora. "Das heißt, wir müssen als Deutschland gar nicht zwingend eine gesamte Wertschöpfungskette beherrschen, um trotzdem am Markt teilzuhaben."
Viel ungenutztes Potenzial bei den Firmen?
Dass KI deutschen Unternehmen auch jenseits der Robotik wirtschaftliche Chancen bietet, zeigt eine KfW-Untersuchung vom September. Mittelständische Unternehmen, die KI einsetzen, weisen demnach im Schnitt ein stärkeres Umsatzwachstum, eine höhere Produktivität und bessere Renditen auf.
Überhaupt scheinen viele Unternehmen hierzulande ihr Potenzial kaum auszuschöpfen. Das geht aus einer Analyse der Unternehmensberatung McKinsey hervor. Zwischen 2019 und 2023 waren gerade einmal 29 von 16.200 untersuchten Firmen - 0,2 Prozent - für 47 Prozent des Produktivitätswachstums in dieser Unternehmensgruppe verantwortlich. Dabei verlaufe die entscheidende Trennlinie nicht zwischen Branchen, betont McKinsey-Experte Jan Krause, sondern "zwischen Mut und Zögern".
Bürokratie bremst Investitionen
Ein Grund für die Zurückhaltung vieler Unternehmen ist nach Einschätzung von ZEW-Ökonom Christian Rammer die Bürokratie. Zu viele Vorschriften, langwierige Genehmigungsverfahren - all das bremse Investitionen, selbst wenn die Nachfrage vorhanden sei. Unternehmen liefen dadurch Gefahr, wichtige Marktchancen zu verpassen. Oder wie Rammer es formuliert: "Bis wir damit durch sind, ist vielleicht der Markt schon wieder weg oder andere waren einfach schneller."
An Wachstumschancen mangelt es Deutschland also nicht. Bleibt nur die Frage, wie sich die Voraussetzungen schaffen lassen, um sie auch zu nutzen.

title: Russland in Afrika: Was der Kreml erreichen will
content_c:
Russischer Einfluss in Afrika: Welche Interessen verfolgt der Kreml?
27. Oktober 2026
Der Konflikt mit dem Westen, ausgelöst durch Russlands umfassende Invasion in der Ukraine, veranlasst den Kreml, Unterstützung in anderen Regionen zu suchen. Afrika ist dabei zu einem Schwerpunkt geworden. Die dort zunehmenden Besuche von Außenminister Sergej Lawrow bezeichnet dessen Sprecherin Maria Sacharowa als eine "historische Rückkehr". Was Russland im 20. Jahrhundert für Afrika getan habe, sei "mit nichts und niemandem vergleichbar", so Sacharowa.
Ägypten wichtigster Partner in Afrika
Seit 2019 findet in Russland alle drei Jahre ein Russland-Afrika-Gipfel statt. Der dritte ist für den 28. und 29. Oktober in Moskau angesetzt. Das Programm konzentriert sich auf die wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit. Weitere Themen reichen von Politik und Sicherheit bis hin zu Wissenschaft und Kultur. Russland arbeitet jedoch nur mit wenigen Staaten, vor allem im Norden des Kontinents, aktiv zusammen, was im Außenhandel zum Ausdruck kommt.
"Obwohl Südafrika nach wie vor die größte Volkswirtschaft Afrikas ist, ist das Handelsvolumen Russlands mit dem Land gering - deutlich niedriger als mit Ägypten und Algerien", sagt Ivan Klyszcz vom Internationalen Zentrum für Verteidigung und Sicherheit (ICDS) in Tallinn und fügt hinzu: "Gerade Ägypten und Algerien sind die Schlüsselpartner Russlands. Ägypten kommt dabei eine wichtige Rolle zu. Russische Diplomaten und Wirtschaftsvertreter versuchen zwar, die Beziehungen auch zu anderen Ländern, vor allem zu Tansania und Äthiopien auszubauen, bislang jedoch ohne nennenswerte Ergebnisse."
Ägypten ist die zweitgrößte Volkswirtschaft auf dem Kontinent. Seit 2021 hat sich das bilaterale Handelsvolumen mehr als verdoppelt und erreichte 2025 laut Angaben des Föderalen Zolldienstes Russlands 10,5 Milliarden US-Dollar. Der wichtigste Treiber sind Lieferungen von russischem Getreide, gefolgt von Erzeugnissen der Metallindustrie. Ägypten liefert vor allem Obst und Gemüse nach Russland.
Ferner gibt es Investitionsprojekte. Russland errichtet ein großes Kernkraftwerk in der ägyptischen Region El-Dabaa an der Mittelmeerküste. Der Bau wird mit einem russischen Kredit von 25 Milliarden US-Dollar finanziert, der etwa 85 Prozent der Kosten abdecken soll.
Ägypten ist eines der wenigen afrikanischen Länder, mit denen Russland über stabile Geschäftsbeziehungen und viel Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit verfügt, meint der Nahostexperte Nikita Smagin. "Langfristig könnte Ägypten für Moskau zum Tor nach Afrika, zu weiteren Märkten werden. Aber Kairo folgt auch eigenen Interessen. Zu hoffen, dass Ägypten nur aus politischer Solidarität Unterstützung leistet, wäre zu optimistisch", sagt er.
Wirtschaftliche Rolle Russlands in Afrika
Laut dem russischen Zolldienst entfielen 2025 etwa 39 Prozent des russisch-afrikanischen Handels auf Ägypten und der Umsatz zwischen Russland und allen 54 Ländern des Kontinents belief sich auf rund 27 Milliarden US-Dollar. Der Anteil Afrikas an Russlands Außenhandel ist somit gering (3,9 Prozent im Jahr 2025) und steht in keinem Verhältnis zur Aufmerksamkeit, die Moskau den Beziehungen zu den Ländern des Kontinents widmet.
Russland ist seinerseits auch kein bedeutender Handelspartner für Afrika. So belief sich das Handelsvolumen mit der Europäischen Union, dem wichtigsten Partner der afrikanischen Länder, im Jahr 2025 auf rund 385 Milliarden US-Dollar. Auch andere Partner liegen laut eigenen Angaben klar vor Russland. Das Handelsvolumen mit China überstieg im Jahr 2025 348 Milliarden US-Dollar, das mit den USA erreichte fast 105 und mit Indien etwa 103 Milliarden US-Dollar.
Die wirtschaftliche Präsenz Russlands sei in Afrika deutlich weniger zu spüren als die Chinas, der USA, traditioneller Akteure wie Frankreich und Großbritannien sowie Indiens, meint Fidel Owusu. Der ghanaische Experte des Analysezentrums Geopolitical Intelligence Services betont: "Bei Handel und Investitionen waren in den letzten Jahren Regionalmächte wie die Türkei und die Vereinigten Arabischen Emirate in Afrika erfolgreicher als Russland."
Auch wenn man auf dem Russland-Afrika-Gipfel viel über Wirtschaft sprechen wird, sind doch die konkreten Pläne wenig beeindruckend. Pawel Kalmytschek, der im russischen Ministerium für wirtschaftliche Entwicklung die Abteilung für bilaterale Zusammenarbeit leitet, erklärte jüngst, bis 2030 wolle man das Handelsvolumen verdoppeln. Selbst wenn dies gelänge, würde Russland im Vergleich etwa zu Deutschland weiter zurückbleiben. Das deutsche Handelsvolumen mit Afrika belief sich laut dem Statistischen Bundesamt (Destatis) im Jahr 2025 auf rund 72 Milliarden US-Dollar.
"Westliche Länder dominieren in strategisch wichtigen Bereichen wie der Rohstoffgewinnung, im Finanzwesen und Energiesektor, auch wenn ihre politische Präsenz in der Region abnimmt", sagt Beverly Ochieng von der Unternehmensberatung Control Risks im Senegal und merkt an: "Russland wird um den Zugang zu kritischen mineralischen Rohstoffen und Energieprojekten konkurrieren. Das sieht man bei Lithium-Projekten in Mali sowie bei Kernenergie-Initiativen auf dem ganzen Kontinent."
Russische Söldner in Afrika
Deutlicher als bei Handel und Investitionen zeigt sich die russische Präsenz in Afrika im Militärbereich. Seit der "Wagner-Gruppe" unterstützen russische Söldner insbesondere die Regime in den instabilen Staaten der Sahelzone. Dafür erhalten die mit ihnen verbundenen Strukturen Zugang zu Rohstoffen. Nach dem Tod des Gründers der "Wagner-Gruppe", Jewgenij Prigoschin, kamen die meisten dieser Operationen unter die Kontrolle des "Afrikakorps", einer Söldnertruppe, die Russlands Verteidigungsministerium geschaffen hat.
Laut dem Congressional Research Service, der Denkfabrik des US-Kongresses, befinden sich die größten russischen Militär-Kontingente in der Zentralafrikanischen Republik, in Mali und Libyen. Es handelt sich jeweils um mehrere tausend Mann. Das "Afrikakorps" will offenbar zudem seine Präsenz in Burkina Faso und Niger ausweiten. Auch in Äquatorialguinea wurden schon russische Söldner gesichtet.
Eine militärische Präsenz sei für Russland aus mehreren Gründen wichtig, betont Irina Filatova von der Universität Kapstadt. "Die Länder haben beträchtliche Vorkommen an Bodenschätzen wie Gold und Uran. Über sie lässt sich Einfluss auf die südlichen Grenzen Europas ausüben, unter anderem in Fragen der Migration und der regionalen Sicherheit. Was Libyen betrifft, so ist das Land als logistischer Knotenpunkt für Verbindungen zum Sahel und nach Zentralafrika von Bedeutung. Über Libyen lassen sich Lieferungen in Länder, die keinen Zugang zum Meer haben, bequem sicherstellen", so die Expertin.
Schließlich ist Russland weiterhin einer der größten Waffenlieferanten für afrikanische Länder, auch wenn die russischen Exporte im Laufe des Ukraine-Krieges zurückgegangen sind. Das Stockholmer Friedensforschungsinstitut (SIPRI) beziffert Moskaus Anteil am afrikanischen Markt für die Jahre 2021–2025 auf 15 Prozent - das ist der dritte Platz hinter den USA (19 Prozent) und China (17 Prozent). In dem Zeitraum 2020–2024 war Russlands Anteil noch höher: Mit 21 Prozent belegte es den ersten Platz, gefolgt von China mit 18 Prozent und den USA mit 16 Prozent.
Was sind Russlands diplomatische Ziele in Afrika
Russland ist für Afrika zwar kein bedeutender Wirtschaftspartner, aber aufgrund von Lieferungen von Nahrungs- und Düngemitteln sowie einer militärische Präsenz in einigen Ländern, ist Moskaus Einfluss in Afrika weitaus größer, als man allein anhand des Handels- und Investitionsvolumens vermuten würde, sagt Ivan Klyszcz vom ICDS.
"Russland misst dem diplomatischen Gewicht Afrikas, dem Kontinent mit den meisten Staaten, große Bedeutung bei. Für Moskau ist vor allem die Unterstützung afrikanischer Länder bei Abstimmungen in der UN-Generalversammlung wichtig. In letzter Zeit gelingt es Russland häufiger, sich diese Unterstützung zu sichern", sagt Fidel Owusu.
Ähnlicher Auffassung ist Irina Filatova: "Die Beziehungen zu Afrika sind für Russland als Beweis sehr wichtig, dafür, dass das Land nicht international isoliert ist. Die russische Führung will zeigen, dass sie auf die Unterstützung eines beträchtlichen Teils der Welt zählen kann, und die afrikanischen Staaten spielen dabei eine große Rolle."
Wahrnehmung Russlands in Afrika
In den letzten Jahren positioniert sich Russland auf der internationalen Bühne als Vertreter der Interessen des Globalen Südens und stellt diesen dem Westen gegenüber, wobei es unter anderem auf das koloniale Erbe verweist.
"Wir wollen mit Afrika zusammenarbeiten, wir arbeiten zusammen und werden weiterhin zusammenarbeiten, allerdings nicht so, wie es die Kolonialherren taten, um an Afrika zu verdienen oder dem Kontinent etwas zu rauben, sondern um uns gemeinsam weiterzuentwickeln", so Russlands Präsident Wladimir Putin jüngst bei einer Tagung des Expertenklubs Waldai.
In manchen Ländern finden Verweise auf die koloniale Vergangenheit Anklang, in anderen nicht, sagt Irina Filatova: "Afrika ist kein Land, sondern ein Kontinent. Es gibt Unterschiede in der Wahrnehmung Russlands sowie in der Art und Weise, wie Russland sich selbst positioniert. Zudem unterscheiden sich die Ansichten der politischen Eliten oft erheblich von denen der einfachen Bürger. In Südafrika beispielsweise wird das russische Narrativ durchaus positiv aufgenommen. In anderen Ländern ist eine antikoloniale Agenda zwar ebenfalls populär, doch wird sie nicht zwangsläufig mit Russland in Verbindung gebracht."
Beverly Ochieng zufolge setzt Russland auch "Soft Power" ein, etwa mit Kulturzentren oder Ausbildungsprogrammen für Journalisten, die auch eine ideologische Schulung umfassen. Gegenüber Russland ließen sich die afrikanischen Staaten aber in erster Linie von eigenen strategischen Interessen leiten, so Ochieng.
Betrachtet man beispielsweise die Dokumente der Afrikanischen Union, des größten Integrationsverbunds des Kontinents, so werden darin wirtschaftliche Entwicklung, Handel und Investitionen als Hauptziele genannt, nicht aber eine Konfrontation mit dem Westen. In diesen Bereichen bietet Russland bislang den afrikanischen Ländern keine Möglichkeiten, die mit denen anderer Akteure vergleichbar sind, betont Ivan Klysch.
Mitarbeit: Antonio Cascais
Adaption aus dem Russischen: Markian Ostaptschuk

title: Колись їх знала вся країна: куди зникли та чим займаються зараз Гайтана, брати Борисенки та інші
content_c:
Колись їх знала вся країна: куди зникли та чим займаються зараз Гайтана, брати Борисенки та інші
Вони збирали зали, очолювали музичні чарти та регулярно з’являлися на телеекранах, але згодом обрали інший шлях. Розповідаємо, як склалося життя колишніх кумирів української публіки.
Український шоубізнес знає чимало артистів, чиї пісні свого часу лунали звідусіль, а обличчя регулярно з’являлися на телеекранах. Проте згодом одні з них відійшли від сцени, інші обрали життя за кордоном, а дехто взагалі змінив професію.
Редакція сайту ТСН.ua розповідає, куди зникли Гайтана, Євгенія Власова, Вадим Олійник, Василіса Фролова, Марія Яремчук і брати Борисенки та чим вони займаються нині.
Гайтана
«Шаленій», «Самотня босса» та «Два вікна» свого часу зробили Гайтану однією з найвпізнаваніших українських співачок. Артистка запам’яталася слухачам незвичайним тембром голосу, запальними композиціями та яскравими виступами. Однак згодом її стало значно менше на українському телебаченні, а нові музичні релізи перестали з’являтися так часто, як на піку популярності.
Під час повномасштабної війни співачка тривалий час не виступала в Україні. У червні 2025 року вона повернулася на батьківщину та дала перший за час великої війни концерт у Києві. Гайтана стала хедлайнеркою фестивалю «Покоління», який відбувся на ВДНГ, і виконала свої найвідоміші пісні. Відео з виступу викликали ностальгію у слухачів, які скучили за артисткою.
Водночас її повернення до української публіки не минулося без дискусій. У 2024 році співачка виступала в Бішкеку, столиці Киргизстану, що викликало неоднозначну реакцію в українців. Попри це, її концерт у Києві засвідчив, що інтерес до колишніх хітів нікуди не зник.
Сьогодні Гайтана не настільки часто з’являється в інформаційному просторі, як раніше. Водночас говорити про остаточне завершення її музичної кар’єри немає підстав: артистка повернулася на сцену та знову зустрілася зі своїми слухачами.
Євгенія Власова
На початку 2000-х пісні Євгенії Власової були добре знайомі українській аудиторії. Її композиції «Ветер надежды» та «Я — живая река» принесли співачці популярність, а сильний голос і сценічний образ зробили її однією з помітних виконавиць того часу.
Проте згодом артистка поступово відійшла від активної музичної кар’єри. На її рішення вплинули особисті обставини та проблеми зі здоров’ям, про які вона раніше розповідала публічно. Після участі в шоу «Танці з зірками» Власова також говорила про емоційне та фізичне виснаження. З початком повномасштабного вторгнення вона виїхала з України разом із донькою, аби подбати про її безпеку, а наприкінці 2023 року повернулася додому.
У період творчої паузи співачка переосмислила своє покликання. Власова розповідала, що працює з людьми через голос, вібрації та звукові практики. Вона називала себе духовною практикинею та пояснювала, що цей напрям відповідає її внутрішнім прагненням.
Однак у серпні 2026 року артистка нагадала про себе музичною прем’єрою. Власова представила оновлену українськомовну версію своєї відомої композиції «Вітер надії». За словами співачки, з роками змінилося її сприйняття пісні, а знайомі слова набули нового, глибшого значення.
Отже, тривала відсутність Власової на сцені не означала остаточного прощання з музикою. Нині виконавиця знову привертає увагу аудиторії, хоча про повноцінне повернення до активного концертного графіка поки не йдеться.
Вадим Олійник
2008 року Вадим Олійник став учасником одного вокального шоу, де познайомився з Володимиром Дантесом. Згодом артисти об’єдналися в дует «ДіО.фільми», який швидко здобув популярність. Їхні пісні «Мне уже 20», «Оля» та «Рингтон» лунали на радіо, а самі виконавці регулярно з’являлися на музичних заходах і телебаченні.
Після шести років спільної творчості гурт припинив існування, а Олійник зосередився на сольній кар’єрі під ім’ям OLEYNIK. Він випускав власні композиції, однак з часом став рідше з’являтися в музичних новинах. Через це в аудиторії могло скластися враження, що співак узагалі залишив шоубізнес.
Насправді Вадим спробував себе в кількох напрямках. Окрім музики, він працює в дубляжі, створює розважальний контент і розвиває власні YouTube-проєкти. Серед них — формати про стосунки та спілкування, а також подкасти. 2026 року він почав розвивати футбольний проєкт.
Окремою сторінкою його життя стало волонтерство після початку повномасштабного вторгнення. А влітку 2025 року Олійник несподівано зустрівся з Дантесом на сцені Atlas Festival. Колишні колеги виконали україномовну версію пісні «Дівчина Оля», чим потішили шанувальників дуету.
Тож Вадим не зник із професійного життя — радше змінив формат роботи. Сьогодні він поєднує творчість із медійними проєктами, дубляжем і спортом, не обмежуючись лише виступами на сцені.
Марія Яремчук
Марія Яремчук стала широко відомою після участі в українському національному відборі на «Євробачення-2013». Уже наступного року вона представляла Україну на міжнародному конкурсі в Копенгагені, де посіла шосте місце з піснею Tick-Tock. Її кар’єра розвивалася стрімко, а участь у «Євробаченні» зробила співачку впізнаваною далеко за межами України.
Однак 2018 року Яремчук оголосила про паузу в концертній діяльності. Відтоді вона стала значно рідше з’являтися на публіці та майже не давала інтерв’ю. Причини відходу від активної сцени були пов’язані з її особистим рішенням і небажанням продовжувати кар’єру в колишньому форматі. Попри очікування прихильників, артистка не поспішала повертатися до регулярних виступів.
Це не означало, що Марія повністю відмовилася від творчості. Після початку повномасштабної війни вона випустила пісні «Щит і меч», «Вона» та «Дорога воїна». А 2023 року Яремчук знову з’явилася на великій сцені — під час фіналу «Євробачення» у Великій Британії, де Україну представляли в інтервал-акті.
Ще одним важливим напрямком її роботи стало документальне кіно. Марія виступила продюсеркою фільму «Яремчук: Незрівнянний світ краси», присвяченого її батькові — легендарному співакові Назарію Яремчуку. Стрічка розповідає про його життя, творчість і внесок в українську музику та стала одним із найпомітніших українських документальних кінопроєктів 2024 року.
У 2026 році про Яремчук знову заговорили після інтерв’ю її кума Олександра Пономарьова. Артист розповів, що Марія нині пише тексти, і високо оцінив її поетичні роботи. Водночас він не зміг підтвердити, чи планує вона повернутися до концертної діяльності.
Брати Борисенки
Олександр і Володимир Борисенки свого часу були одними з найвідоміших близнюків українського шоубізнесу. Вони здобули популярність завдяки участі у вокальному шоу, випускали пісні, виступали на концертах і мали чималу аудиторію прихильників. Їхній дует асоціювався з молодіжною попмузикою кінця 2000-х і початку 2010-х років.
Згодом брати відійшли від музичної кар’єри та почали будувати професійне життя в інших сферах. На відміну від багатьох колишніх учасників талант-шоу, вони не стали регулярно повертатися на телебачення чи підтримувати популярність за допомогою світських заходів. Саме тому інформації про них у медіа стало значно менше.
Однак обидва знайшли заняття, які відповідають їхнім нинішнім інтересам. Володимир Борисенко присвятив себе соціальній роботі та благодійності. Він розвиває проєкт «Жити назустріч», спрямований на допомогу ветеранам і їхню адаптацію до цивільного життя, а також долучається до благодійних ініціатив на підтримку українських військових.
Олександр натомість працює в креативній індустрії. Він займається дизайном, відеомонтажем і режисурою. Сам артист спростовував чутки про роботу в IT, наголошуючи, що його діяльність пов’язана саме з візуальним контентом і творчими проєктами.
У травні 2025 року брати знову привернули увагу публіки, коли з’явилися в сюжеті на телебаченні. Тоді вони розповіли, як змінилися за роки поза сценою та чим живуть нині.
Нагадаємо, нещодавно редакція сайту ТСН.ua розповіла, на яких машинах їздять українські зірки та скільки вони коштують.

Це не означало, що Марія повністю відмовилася від творчості. Після початку повномасштабної війни вона випустила пісні «Щит і меч», «Вона» та «Дорога воїна». А 2023 року Яремчук знову з’явилася на великій сцені — під час фіналу «Євробачення» у Великій Британії, де Україну представляли в інтервал-акті.
Ще одним важливим напрямком її роботи стало документальне кіно. Марія виступила продюсеркою фільму «Яремчук: Незрівнянний світ краси», присвяченого її батькові — легендарному співакові Назарію Яремчуку. Стрічка розповідає про його життя, творчість і внесок в українську музику та стала одним із найпомітніших українських документальних кінопроєктів 2024 року.
У 2026 році про Яремчук знову заговорили після інтерв’ю її кума Олександра Пономарьова. Артист розповів, що Марія нині пише тексти, і високо оцінив її поетичні роботи. Водночас він не зміг підтвердити, чи планує вона повернутися до концертної діяльності.
Брати Борисенки
Олександр і Володимир Борисенки свого часу були одними з найвідоміших близнюків українського шоубізнесу. Вони здобули популярність завдяки участі у вокальному шоу, випускали пісні, виступали на концертах і мали чималу аудиторію прихильників. Їхній дует асоціювався з молодіжною попмузикою кінця 2000-х і початку 2010-х років.
Згодом брати відійшли від музичної кар’єри та почали будувати професійне життя в інших сферах. На відміну від багатьох колишніх учасників талант-шоу, вони не стали регулярно повертатися на телебачення чи підтримувати популярність за допомогою світських заходів. Саме тому інформації про них у медіа стало значно менше.
Однак обидва знайшли заняття, які відповідають їхнім нинішнім інтересам. Володимир Борисенко присвятив себе соціальній роботі та благодійності. Він розвиває проєкт «Жити назустріч», спрямований на допомогу ветеранам і їхню адаптацію до цивільного життя, а також долучається до благодійних ініціатив на підтримку українських військових.
Олександр натомість працює в креативній індустрії. Він займається дизайном, відеомонтажем і режисурою. Сам артист спростовував чутки про роботу в IT, наголошуючи, що його діяльність пов’язана саме з візуальним контентом і творчими проєктами.
У травні 2025 року брати знову привернули увагу публіки, коли з’явилися в сюжеті на телебаченні. Тоді вони розповіли, як змінилися за роки поза сценою та чим живуть нині.
Нагадаємо, нещодавно редакція сайту ТСН.ua розповіла, на яких машинах їздять українські зірки та скільки вони коштують.

title: В Харькове в результате удара пятеро пострадавших: горели дома, гаражи и производственное здание
content_c:
В ночь на 28 октября российские войска атаковали Основянский район Харькова с помощью реактивного дрона. В результате удара ранения получили пять человек, в том числе четырёхлетний ребёнок, сообщает Государственная служба по чрезвычайным ситуациям (ГСЧС) в своём Telegram-канале. Там также опубликованы кадры последствий вражеской атаки.
Отмечается, что в результате удара возник крупный пожар площадью 2500 кв. м. Огонь охватил многоквартирный и частный дома, хозяйственные постройки и производственное здание. Также повреждены многоэтажные дома, гаражи и автомобили.
«Под угрозой повторных ударов спасатели совместно с другими службами ликвидируют последствия. Психологи ГСЧС оказали помощь пострадавшим», — говорится в сообщении.
Напомним, 26 октября российские войска нанесли ракетные удары по Новобаварскому району Харькова. В результате атаки погибли два человека. Также были повреждены десять гаражей, четыре частных дома, четыре многоэтажки и здание детского сада.
Также в четверг, 22 октября, россияне атаковали Центральный рынок в Лозовой Харьковской области дронами-ракетами «Бандероль» и беспилотниками «Шахед». В результате обстрела погибли два человека, ещё 34 получили ранения.
Ранее, 20 октября, российские войска атаковали ракетами частный сектор Новобаварского района Харькова. В результате удара девять местных жителей получили контузии и осколочные ранения.
О том, как харьковчане приспосабливаются к жизни под ежедневными ударами, в статье ZN.UA «Харьков — город-крепость. Стратегия выживания» рассказывает журналистка Оксана Нечепоренко.
