description: Harry Kane is the humble 'anti-superstar' who defied doubters to achieve Ballon d'Or greatness, says chief football writer Phil McNulty.
content:
How Kane defied doubters to become world's best
- Published
Harry Kane has taken the scenic route to the Ballon d'Or - a road littered with doubts and diversions, but one that eventually led to the ultimate destination: being crowned as the world's best player.
The 33-year-old's glory at the London Palladium on Monday is fitting reward for an exemplary career that has seen records fall at his feet for England, Tottenham Hotspur and Bayern Munich.
Kane is England's top goalscorer with 91 goals. He has 125 England caps, joint-highest with Peter Shilton. He is Spurs' record scorer with 280 goals in 435 appearances. He scored a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for Bayern Munich and England during the 2025–26 season.
This is the Kane of recent vintage, the world-class striker and complete footballer who beat Real Madrid and France striker Kylian Mbappe, as well as Spain's teenage Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal, to the sport's biggest personal honour.
Kane's humility has seen him described as an 'anti-superstar' and his achievement has been commended both inside and outside the football world.
One post on social media from Kane as he celebrated the greatest moment of his career said it all: "Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise."
And yet, Kane's journey was not always smooth.
It was one that started with loan moves around the lower divisions with Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City before he developed into a great for club and country.
The same Kane sat on the bench on loan at Leicester City – alongside future England team-mate Jamie Vardy – when the Foxes lost a dramatic Championship play-off at Watford in May 2013.
Kane went through hard schools and hard times away from his more familiar environment at Spurs, joining Orient on loan as a 17-year-old in January 2011, playing 18 games with nine starts and scoring five goals.
He joined Millwall in similar circumstances a year later, with some behind the scenes at Spurs fearing the traditionally hostile atmosphere at the New Den might intimidate the teenager, but he acquitted himself well, scoring nine goals in 24 starts.
Former Spurs manager Tim Sherwood said: "I used to watch Harry a lot at Millwall and it was an intimidating atmosphere. I remember overhearing one of our scouts come and talk to Harry Redknapp - who was Spurs manager at the time - and say: 'We need to get Harry Kane out of Millwall, it's no good for him there'.
"I went straight in and said: 'This is the perfect atmosphere for him'."
Kane made his Spurs debut in August 2012 before a spell at Norwich City, where he failed to score in three starts and suffered a serious foot injury.
It was an unhappy time but Chris Hughton, the former Spurs defender who was manager at Carrow Road, said: "What I saw in him was a desire to do well. Did I see him having the mobility and flexibility he has in his game now? Probably not. He was a very good finisher. He would stay out after training for half an hour every day, left foot, right foot."
Next stop was Leicester City between February and May 2013, when he made five starts and scored two goals, a stint best remembered for that dramatic Championship play-off game when Troy Deeney scored for Watford to send them to Wembley seconds after Anthony Knockaert's penalty was saved by Manuel Almunia.
Kane was not even selected in Leicester's starting line-up, only being sent on after 61 minutes. And who was alongside him on the bench? Vardy, who later won the Premier league with the Foxes and played alongside Kane for England.
He later admitted this was a time of self-doubt, saying: "That was probably the time in my career where it was the hardest - I was 19 and I was thinking, 'If I can't play for Norwich or for Leicester, even in the Championship, then how I am going to get back and play for Tottenham?'"

  - Published23 hours ago
- Quiz: Kane and who else? Name every men's Ballon d'Or winner 
  - Published20 hours ago
It is testimony to Kane's strength of character, even as a youngster, that he not only returned to Spurs but left for Bayern Munich in August 2023 as one of their greatest ever players.
Even at Spurs, Kane's superb record always carried the qualification that he never won a trophy, a stick used to unfairly beat a player whose remarkable consistency and approach marked him down as the consummate professional.
Kane has put that right spectacularly at Bayern, winning the Bundesliga twice, the move propelling him to the level of global superstar, giving him the profile and platform to win the Ballon d'Or - the first English player to win the trophy since Michael Owen in 2001 and the fifth overall.
Former England midfielder Danny Murphy told BBC Sport recently: "He's a born goalscorer. He's a super professional. He's technically brilliant. He's been an absolute credit to himself and his family in the way he's conducted himself and the longevity he's had in his career."
There is still that one space on his roll of honour, namely success with England after losses in two Euros finals and two World Cup semi-final defeats, but who would bet against Kane being fit and motivated enough to have one last crack at Euro 2028 in the UK and Ireland.
Kane is now at the peak of his powers and fitness, not just a goalscoring machine but the complete player capable of dropping deep into midfield to play the sort of breathtaking defence splitting pass exemplified by Alphonso Davies' goal against Arsenal in the recent Champions League game.
One of Kane's illustrious predecessors in England's number nine shirt, Alan Shearer, told BBC Radio 5 Live: "It was so well deserved because he hasn't had things all his own way. He's had to go round it the hard way. He had to start off the hard way by someone telling him, 'You're not quite good enough, you're going to have to work a lot harder to get to where you want to'.
"He did that. He went out on loan and worked harder than anyone else. He's got to the very, very top and now he's the best player in the world and that's what dedication does for you. It's a message to everyone.
"Harry said it in his speech - that if you're told you're not good enough, then go and try again and work harder. He did that and look where he is now. He's been scoring goals at a phenomenal rate for so many years now and he deserved it."
Shearer added: "I think the best thing for me is how humble Harry is. Footballers are like movie stars nowadays. You see them walking down the red carpet and some of them are in sunglasses when it's pitch black and eight o'clock at night. Harry is just normal, as normal as they come."
Once the celebrations die down, it will be back to business for the humble superstar, with Bayern playing Magdeburg in the German DFB Pokal second round on Wednesday before the big home fixture against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday evening.
Kane's career has not been without its obstacles but he remains as focused as ever to conquer whatever is placed in front of him by Bayern Munich and England.

title: What Marco Rubio’s sidestepping of New Delhi says about the US’s stance on India
content_c:
When the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, visited India for the second time this year, headlines concentrated on who he met and where he went.
The fact that Rubio bypassed New Delhi and did not meet the prime minister, Narendra Modi, during his trip last week, and instead traveled to the financial capital, Mumbai, where he met India’s foreign minister, Subrahmanyam Jaishankar (pictured top with Rubio), and business leaders, did not go unnoticed. Nor did his decision to travel to Jamnagar, the small Gujarati town that is home to Reliance Industries’ colossal oil refinery complex.
Bilateral ties between the two countries have come under strain under the second Trump administration, particularly over tariffs and India’s purchase of Russian oil. Yet, Rubio’s return to India just five months after his first visit as secretary of state signals that the country remains useful for president Donald Trump’s ambitions after all.
As director of the South Asia Program at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, Milan Vaishnav has spent a decade tracking India’s place in the world, particularly its ties with the US. Vaishnav has described Trump 2.0 as “unbound” marking a new era in India-US relations.
Tracking foreign affairs, he told me, is a minefield right now. From the White House’s transactional approach to global alliances, ongoing conflicts in the Middle East and consequential elections around the world, politics is changing at a pace that means all predictions are off the table. “I think anyone who tells you they know exactly what is going on and how it fits into their neat theory of the world is lying to you,” says Vaishnav.
I asked him about the many confusing aspects of the US-India relationship, from the hostile political rhetoric to the US embrace of Pakistan, as well as Rubio’s latest visit.
Trump the deal-maker
Ahead of Rubio’s visit, several commentators noted the secretary of state’s “unusual” itinerary. Vaishnav thought the pre-visit chatter about Rubio skipping Delhi to visit Mumbai and Jamnagar was overblown. “Not every bilateral meeting has to take place in a national capital,” he says.
But that doesn’t mean it wasn’t noteworthy. “I do think the choice of venues was intentional. This administration and, particularly, this president, sees foreign policy through the lens of ‘deal-making’. And if you’re trying to drum up business deals, what better place to visit than Mumbai?” he says.
The Jamnagar visit, where Rubio met Mukesh Ambani, the chair of Reliance, also indicates some politicking. “At a time when petrol prices are extremely high in the United States and are likely to be a major issue in the 3 November midterm elections, the administration wants to show that it is doing everything it can to bring them down. India is a major consumer of oil, but it is also a major exporter of refined petroleum products,” says Vaishnav. “One of Rubio’s objectives was to encourage Reliance and, by extension, India to process more Venezuelan crude [oil],” he added.
While this could present an opportunity for India to advance relations, it’s not a given: the US president remains, after all – and to put it lightly – mercurial.
“The biggest plot twist for me has been the Trump administration’s embrace of Pakistan after the May 2025 conflict with India,” says Vaishnav. Pakistan’s standing in Washington had eroded over the years, especially under Joe Biden, who left office without ever having made a presidential phone call to his counterpart in Pakistan. “Many officials in Congress had grown exhausted with Pakistan’s double game, speaking the language of partnership on the one hand while undermining US interests on the other,” says Vaishnav.
But, after coming to power the second time, Trump thanked the country for its help in nabbing a suspect linked to a 2021 bombing in Afghanistan that killed 13 US service members. This reversal in Pakistan’s fortunes gathered pace after the May conflict with India, which Trump took credit for ending. In June, he welcomed Asim Munir, Pakistan’s army chief, to the White House, after Munir called for the president to be nominated for the Nobel peace prize.
“I chalk up the reversal to a few factors: Trump’s well-known strongman envy, Pakistan’s savvy diplomacy, and the prospect of energy and crypto deals involving members of Trump’s inner circle,” says Vaishnav. For him, it isyet another demonstration of how much weight Trump places on deals, transactions and short-term wins. “For New Delhi, this means Modi’s personal rapport with Trump and 25 years of investment in the bilateral relationship offer no guarantee against a 180-degree reversal in US policy,” he adds.
In a recent piece, Vaishnav’s colleague Sameer Lalwani pointed out that the US relationship with India remains more resilient than the political rhetoric may suggest with quiet, but nonetheless strategic, progress being made.
As Lalwani points out, bilateral trade reached a record high between India and the US in 2025; nearly $68bn worth of AI infrastructure investment in India has been pledged by US technology companies; and the two countries have carried out record number of joint military exercises this year.
The way forward
Despite these wins, in terms of future bilateral relations, “there are at least three reasons for caution,” warns Vaishnav. First, he points to the onslaught of US actions that have dented Indian interests. Trump had imposed a punitive 50% tariff on India in 2025, which was reduced to 18% earlier this year, but without a comprehensive trade deal being reached. Second, on immigration, the White House’s H-1B visa and green card restrictions have disproportionately affected Indian workers in Silicon Valley.
“This has created a real trust deficit on the Indian side, and with good reason,” says Vaishnav. The frustration was on display earlier this month, when New Delhi branded remarks made by the US vice-president, JD Vance, about Indian professionals as “deeply offensive”. Furthermore, Vaishnav argues that while governments and private sector firms might be great at making announcements, they’re not always a guarantee of delivery.
His final caution is how political tensions can have a chilling effect. The trade negotiations offer a telling example: in January, the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, blamed the lack of a trade deal on Modi’s failure to phone Trump, a characterisation that New Delhi has disputed. Vaishnav says: “Much of the progress we are seeing is the product of decisions made years ago. It is one thing to keep existing projects moving, but turbulence in the relationship could make new initiatives a heavier lift.”
If India is serious about making its ambition to be a global powerhouse a reality, Vaishnav thinks there’s a clearcut way to win. “I would argue that the most important investment is political – ensuring India remains a robust, inclusive, participatory democracy,” he says. “On the economic front, India has made massive new investments in physical and digital infrastructure. But the returns on those investments will be limited unless the government doubles down on reforms: more efficient dispute resolution, an impartial legal system, even-handed tax enforcementand regulatory certainty.”
Ultimately, neither side can afford to treat the other as expendable. The test now is whether strategic foundations can hold at a time of global political upheaval.
What else we’re reading about
Student protests | Bikaner House, one of Delhi’s premier arts venues, asked visual artist Raihan Vadra to remove from his show more than 70 photographs that featured recent student protests. Vadra, the son of the Congress leader, Priyanka Gandhi, defended his work and also refused a request to remove images featuring the national flag. In a press statement, the venue said certain photos were “inconsistent” with its policy.
Fashion | Designer Sabyasachi Mukherjee, celebrated for his maximalist aesthetic, hosted a Diwali party at New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art. In September, he unveiled a high-jewellery collection inspired by the Byzantine, in collaboration with the museum.
Air pollution | Emergency measures, including a ban on coal-fired tandoors in restaurants and restrictions on diesel generators, have come into effect in Delhi, as air quality dropped to the poor category at the onset of the annual pollution season.
Guest shelf
A recommendation from someone with great taste
Film-maker Ritu Sarin, director of the annual Dharamshala international film festival, which runs from 29 October to 1 November, suggests a film from this year’s lineup:
“Shot over three years on real locations, Anmol Sidhu’s sophomore feature, Flowers of Acacia, follows wedding orchestra dancers in rural Punjab with a gaze that allows all the large brutalities and smaller intimacies to shine through. Sidhu’s confident, consummate grasp of the medium is on full display in terrifying scenes that stretch to the edge of what is palatable. The camera refuses to look away.”
Count it
A number worth knowing
7,633
That’s the number of trees Mumbai’s municipal authorities authorised to be felled over five months this year, to make way for development works, according to the Indian Express. Of these, about 3,500 will be permanently removed, while the rest will be replanted elsewhere.
Vibe check
Prarthna Singh has consistently placed the female identity at the heart of her artistic practice, documenting Indian women’s aspirations and acts of rebellion in male-dominated spaces. When commissioned to photograph rkivecity’s menswear line, made from discarded clothes reworked into new garments, she turned that same gaze outward. The setting was the acclaimed 151-year-old Mayo College boys’ school in Ajmer, Rajasthan – Singh attended the linked girls’ school, and credits it with shaping her rebellious spirit.
“I was thinking about how I could bring a sense of intimacy and camaraderie of boarding-school life to the images, because that exists,” she told me. One image shows a pair of hands holding another boy’s jacket, the faces left out of the frame, so the garment stands in for the familiarity they share. Seeing this work against the backdrop of students taking to the streets to fight for their rights lends the series a lasting significance. “This was just my way of showing all of this is connected. These worlds are not existing separately,” said Singh.

title: Seychellen, La Digue: Deutscher Tourist tot aufgefunden
content_c:
Von Ehefrau vermisst gemeldet Deutscher Tourist auf Seychellen tot aufgefunden
Ein deutscher Tourist ist offenbar unter bislang ungeklärten Umständen im Urlaub auf den Seychellen gestorben. Der 30-jährige Mann habe sein Hotel auf der Insel La Digue am Montag gegen 21.00 Uhr Ortszeit (19.00 Uhr MEZ) verlassen, um trotz Dunkelheit eine Schwimmbrille zu suchen, die er an einem Strand vergessen hatte, wie die örtliche Polizei mitteilte.
Nachdem der Mann nicht ins Hotel zurückgekehrt sei, habe seine Ehefrau die Behörden informiert. Die Leiche des Deutschen sei am Nachmittag von einem Suchtrupp in einem felsigen Gebiet abseits eines zum Anse Coco Beach führenden Wanderwegs gefunden worden.
Was genau passiert ist, ist bislang unklar. Die Polizei teilte mit, sie habe Untersuchungen eingeleitet, um die Todesursache zu ermitteln. Das Ehepaar war Angaben zufolge am 25. Oktober für einen Kurzurlaub auf den Seychellen eingetroffen und hatte geplant, am 28. Oktober abzufliegen.
Die Inselgruppe im Indischen Ozean rund 1800 Kilometer vor der Küste Kenias ist beliebt für ihr klares, türkisfarbenes Wasser, Korallenriffe und weiße Sandstrände. Die rund zehn Quadratkilometer große Insel La Digue mit rund 2000 Einwohnern liegt etwa 45 Kilometer nordöstlich der Hauptinsel Mahé und ist bekannt für ihre Granitfelsen, traumhaften Strände und traditionellen Ochsenkarren.
description: Ein 30-jähriger deutscher Tourist wollte offenbar nur seine Schwimmbrille suchen, die er am Strand auf einer Insel der Seychellen verloren hatte. Er kehrte jedoch nicht ins Hotel zurück.

title: Atommüll-Endlager: In weiteren Bundesländern soll nicht mehr gesucht werden
content_c:
Suche nach Standort Atommüll-Endlager - weitere Bundesländer sind raus
Die Suche nach einem Endlager für den hochradioaktiven Atommüll in Deutschland wird konkreter. Die zuständigen Fachleute haben die geeigneten Gebiete weiter eingegrenzt - auf weniger als fünf Prozent der Landesfläche.
Auf der Suche nach einem Endlager für den Müll aus deutschen Atomkraftwerken haben die zuständigen Fachleute die deutsche Landesfläche auf nun weniger als fünf Prozent eingegrenzt. In diesen Gebieten hält die Bundesgesellschaft für Endlagerung (BGE) laut einer Pressemitteilung die geologischen Bedingungen grundsätzlich für geeignet.
Damit ist nun die gesamte Landesfläche in Bearbeitung oder bewertet. Die Bundesländer Rheinland-Pfalz, Hessen, Berlin, Sachsen, Hamburg und das Saarland sind dabei nicht mehr Teil der laufenden Suche. Zunächst hatten Nachrichtenagenturen Hamburg nicht gelistet. Ein Pressesprecher der Behörde bestätigte jedoch inzwischen, dass Hamburg nicht mehr in Betracht gezogen wird. Das letzte Wort für die Auswahl des Standortes hat aber der Bundestag.
Fläche immer weiter eingegrenzt
2020 hatte die bundeseigene Gesellschaft zunächst in einem Bericht 90 solcher Gebiete ausgewiesen, bei denen eine weitere Prüfung lohnen könnte. Dies waren knapp 54 Prozent der Fläche Deutschlands.
Das Saarland war den Angaben zufolge bereits 2020 herausgefallen, Rheinland-Pfalz schied 2025 aus, in diesem Jahr neu aussortiert wurden Sachsen, Hamburg, Berlin und Hessen.
Die übrigen Gebiete werden im weiteren Verfahren weiter eingegrenzt. Die Ergebnisse werden auf der Internetseite der BGE als interaktive Karte veröffentlicht.
Geologische Sicherheit hat Vorrang
Bei der Suche wird die geologische Sicherheit der Teilgebiete in einem wissenschaftsbasierten Verfahren schrittweise analysiert. Bei jedem Prüfschritt werden die Sicherheitsanforderungen erhöht, weshalb in der Folge immer mehr Gebiete ausscheiden.
Das wichtigste Werkzeug für die Einengung sind laut BGE sogenannte repräsentative vorläufige Sicherheitsuntersuchungen. Hier wird auf Basis existierender geologischer Daten und Geodaten geprüft, inwieweit der sichere Einschluss der hoch radioaktiven Abfälle unter den jeweiligen geologischen Gegebenheiten erwartet werden kann. Generell gelten Granit, Salz und Ton als potenziell geeignete Gesteinsarten für das angestrebte unterirdische Endlager.
Einengung auf Regionen erst Ende 2027
Die jetzt neu veröffentlichten Arbeitsstände sind noch keine verbindlichen Ergebnisse, weil die Einengung der Teilgebiete auf Standortregionen erst Ende 2027 erfolgt. Nach einer eingehenden Prüfung durch Wissenschaftler und das BASE entscheidet dann der Gesetzgeber, also der Bundestag, wo es in der zweiten Phase weitergeht.
Bis spätestens 2050 soll ein Lager für rund 27.000 Kubikmeter hochradioaktiven Atommüll gefunden werden, der in mehr als 60 Jahren Atomkraft angefallen ist. Der Standort soll Sicherheit für eine Million Jahre bieten.

title: Не лише шарлотка: рецепти яблучних пирогів, які варто спекти цієї осені
content_c:
Не лише шарлотка: рецепти яблучних пирогів, які варто спекти цієї осені
Осінь - час, аби готувати з яблук ароматну домашню випічку, яка наповнює оселю запахом кориці та запечених фруктів.
Восени яблука стають одним із найпопулярніших інгредієнтів для домашньої випічки — соковиті, ароматні та з приємною кислинкою, вони чудово доповнюють пироги й пиріжки. З ними навіть найпростіше тісто перетворюється на смачний десерт, а кориця та ваніль додають випічці особливого осіннього аромату.
ТСН.ua підготував три прості рецепти смачної випічки з яблуками.
Класична шарлотка
Інгредієнти:
- 4 яйця
- 180 г цукру
- 180 г борошна
- 4 середні яблука
- 1 ч. л. розпушувача
- 1 ч. л. кориці
- дрібка солі
Приготування
- Яблука очистіть від шкірки, видаліть серцевину і наріжте тонкими скибочками.
- Яйця збийте з цукром і дрібкою солі до світлої пишної маси. Поступово додайте просіяне борошно і обережно перемішайте лопаткою. Всипте розпушувач.
- Форму діаметром приблизно 22–24 см змастіть маслом. Викладіть яблука, посипте корицею та залийте тістом.
- Випікайте шарлотку в розігрітій до 180°C духовці приблизно 35–45 хв. Готовність перевірте дерев’яною шпажкою.
Насипний яблучний пиріг
Інгредієнти:
- 1 кг яблук
- 160 г борошна
- 160 г манної крупи
- 150 г цукру
- 1,5 ч. л. розпушувача
- 1 ч. л. кориці
- 120 г холодного вершкового масла
- дрібка солі
Приготування:
Яблука натріть на великій тертці. Увесь сік не відтискайте - він допоможе сухим шарам пропектися.
Змішайте борошно, манку, цукор, розпушувач, корицю та сіль. Розділіть суху суміш на три частини, а яблука — на дві.
Форму для випікання застеліть пергаментом. Викладіть перший шар сухої суміші, розподіліть половину яблук. Потім знову суху суміш і решту яблук. Завершальним має бути сухий шар.
Холодне вершкове масло натріть на великій тертці й рівномірно розподіліть зверху.
Випікайте за температури 180°C приблизно 50–60 хв, поки верх не стане золотистим. Готовність перевірте дерев’яною шпажкою.
Пиріг із карамелізованими яблуками
Інгредієнти для начинки:
- 4 середні яблука
- 50 г цукру
- 40 г вершкового масла
- ½ ч. л. кориці
Інгредієнти для тіста:
- 2 яйця;
- 120 г цукру;
- 120 г борошна;
- 80 мл молока;
- 60 г розтопленого вершкового масла;
- 1 ч. л. розпушувача;
- 1 пакетик ванільного цукру;
- дрібка солі.
Приготування:
- Яблука очистіть, видаліть серцевину та наріжте шматочками. На сковороді розтопіть половину вершкового масла, додайте цукор і яблука. Готуйте на середньому вогні 5–8 хв - поки яблука трохи не пом’якшають і вкриються карамельним сиропом. Наприкінці додайте корицю.
- Для тіста збийте яйця із цукром і ванільним цукром. Додайте молоко та розтоплене масло. Додайте борошно, розпушувач і сіль, перемішайте до однорідності.
- Викладіть яблука разом із сиропом у змащену форму. Зверху рівномірно розподіліть тісто.
- Випікайте за температури 180°C приблизно 35–45 хв. . Перевірте готовність шпажкою.
Нагадаємо, ми ділилися рецептом печених яблук із начинкою.

title: Пакет готов, но оружие не отправляют: Италия вновь отложила передачу помощи Украине
content_c:
Премьер-министр Италии Джорджа Мелони приостановила выделение тринадцатого пакета военной помощи Украине в ожидании промежуточных выборов в США, сообщило издание Il Giornale d'Italia.
По данным издания, новый пакет уже готов к отправке, однако после нескольких отсрочек его передачу так и не назначили на конкретную дату. Последняя итальянская поставка военной помощи Украине состоялась десять месяцев назад.
Сначала решение по новому пакету ожидали в июле, затем в сентябре, позже его отложили до съезда партии «Лига», а теперь ориентиром стали промежуточные выборы в США 3 ноября.
При этом не уточняется, какой именно результат американских выборов мог бы повлиять на решение Рима. Также нет данных о том, что помощь будет отправлена сразу после голосования.
Под угрозой также оказалось обязательство, которое Мелони взяла перед президентом Франции Эммануэлем Макроном и президентом Украины Владимиром Зеленским.
Об отмене соглашения или разрыве отношений с Парижем и Киевом речь не идет, однако сроки выполнения обязательства остаются неопределенными.
Как пишет издание, отсутствие конкретной даты новой поставки подрывает доверие и к заверениям Италии о продолжении поддержки Украины. В то же время в правительстве официально продолжают настаивать, что поддержка Украины будет продолжаться, однако не объясняют, когда именно будет отправлена новая помощь и что именно до сих пор мешает принять окончательное решение.
Напомним, что вице-премьер-министра Италии Маттео Сальвини переизбрали лидером ультраправой партии «Лига», входящей в состав правящей коалиции. После переизбрания он планирует потребовать от правительства прекращения военной и финансовой помощи Украине.

title: В Польщі розмістять центр техобслуговування ракет Patriot – Міноборони США
content_c:
Уряд США у координації з компанією Lockheed Martin та європейськими союзниками, оголосив про вибір Польщі для розміщення європейського центру технічного обслуговування ракет Patriot Advanced Capability-3 (PAC-3), повідомляє пресслужба Міністерства оборони США.
Очікується, що цей новий центр буде базуватися на міцній трансатлантичній промисловій співпраці, а інтеграцію критично важливого ланцюга поставок очолюватимуть Німеччина, Нідерланди та Швеція.
"Забезпечення потреб військовослужбовців – у будь-який час і в будь-якому місці – саме так ми стримуємо наших супротивників і зміцнюємо колективну оборону. Сьогоднішнє оголошення втілює партнерство в життя. Інвестуючи національні ресурси у створення цього критично важливого потенціалу забезпечення на Східному фронті НАТО, союзники надсилають чіткий сигнал: Альянс є єдиним, серйозно ставиться до стримування і готовий підкріпити свої слова діями", – заявив заступник міністра оборони з питань закупівель та забезпечення Майкл П. title: Donald Trump's biggest economic problem looks strangely familiar
content_c:
Donald Trump's biggest economic problem looks strangely familiar
- Published
The White House is confronting a familiar dilemma. The economic numbers aren't necessarily bad - but the public mood is.
It's a disconnect that haunted Joe Biden in 2024, when solid headline data failed to convince many voters that the economy was working for them.
Now, Donald Trump faces a version of the same challenge.
During the 2024 campaign, Trump promised voters swift relief from rising prices.
"When I win, I will immediately bring prices down," he said.
Delivering on that promise has proved harder than expected.
Economic growth is holding up, unemployment remains low and the stock market is near record highs.
Yet the final inflation report ahead of the midterm elections confirms what voters already know: prices remain high.
The causes are different. Biden was grappling with the aftermath of the Covid pandemic. Trump faces higher energy prices linked to the US-Israel conflict with Iran and the fallout from some of his own trade and immigration policies.
The political reality, however, is much the same. Voters are not judging the economy by GDP figures or record highs on the stock market. They are judging it by what they pay at the supermarket, petrol prices and whether they can keep up with the bills.
Numbers only tell part of the story
US economic growth of 2.2% would be respectable by the standards of many wealthy economies. Germany, for example, has struggled to generate comparable momentum. And a stable US unemployment rate of 4.2% hardly suggests an economy in freefall.
Trump argues that he inherited an economic mess from Biden, and points to strong growth, investment and stock market performance as evidence that his policies are working.
Following the most recent inflation report, White House spokesman Matthew Middleton said the administration's "aggressive, pro-growth economic agenda" had blunted "Biden's inflation crisis".
Larry Kudlow, a Trump ally and economic commentator, has described the current expansion as "the greatest story never told", external, arguing that "nobody is getting fired".
- US inflation rises more than expected - here's what is happening with prices 
  - Published14 October
But voters appear to be reading a different story - one in which Trump won the presidency promising to tackle the cost of living, only for prices to keep rising.
Part of the problem is that wage increases have not kept pace with prices. Average hourly earnings have risen 3% over the last year, while consumer prices have increased 3.7%.
That helps explain why polls continue to show voters giving Trump poor marks for his handling of the economy.
Same language, different meanings
For Democrats, the dynamic feels familiar.
Celinda Lake, a veteran Democratic pollster, says the problem begins with the way economists and voters use the same language to mean different things.
"When economists say inflation comes down, they mean the rate of increase has come down," she says.
"When voters say inflation has come down, they mean the price has returned to what it was. Well, of course, it never returns to what it was."
The Biden administration spent much of 2024 highlighting low unemployment, solid growth and falling inflation. However, many voters remained focused on the higher prices they faced every day.
Lake, who advised Biden's 2020 campaign but was not involved in the 2024 race, says voters judge the economy through personal experience, not economic indicators.
"You can't argue with people about their own lived reality," she says.
That may help explain why Trump's challenge looks so similar to Biden's.
The Trump effect
Biden's critics blamed him for inflation. But he could point to forces largely outside his control, including the pandemic and its supply chain aftershocks.
Trump has less room to do that.
Some economists argue that today's higher prices are at least partly the result of his own policies, including tariffs, as well as the economic fallout from the US-Israel war with Iran.
"The inflation is clearly traceable to Donald Trump," says Peter Morici, a University of Maryland economist who aligns with Republicans.
"It's his tariffs and the war. People know that. They see it."
Trump's "Liberation Day" tariffs, announced in April 2025, have added to costs for consumers.
A study by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York found the tariffs increased consumer goods prices by about 2.9%.
The impact might have been larger if Trump hadn't later paused some tariffs, struck new trade deals and been blocked by the Supreme Court from using emergency powers to impose many others.
Then came another shock. Conflict with Iran pushed oil prices higher, lifting the cost of petrol and putting fresh pressure on household budgets.
The White House points to tax cuts, job growth and lower prescription drug costs as evidence that the administration is delivering for American families. And it is increasingly embracing policies aimed at easing pressures.
Trump has called for a cap on credit card interest rates and floated the idea of a $5,000 payment to American adults if Republicans retain control of Congress.
The measures reflect a political reality familiar to both parties: when voters are anxious about prices, arguments about solid growth and low unemployment are rarely enough.
Biden never found a way to bridge the gap between economic performance and economic sentiment. The question heading into the midterms is whether Trump can.
If recent political history is any guide, perceptions of the economy may matter more than the economic data itself.

  - Published12 October
  - Published15 October

title: Chancellor targets cost of living crisis in budget for a ‘difficult moment’
content_c:
John Healey has acknowledged the UK faces a “difficult moment” but insisted he would put the country on a better path as he delivers his first budget on Wednesday against a turbulent global economic backdrop.
But despite the international uncertainty, the chancellor will signal “fresh hope for the future” as he attempts to sound a more optimistic note, by providing households with breathing space from rising cost of living pressures.
The budget, which will be interpreted as a signal of Andy Burnham’s intent, is nevertheless expected to be a relatively modest affair as Healey grapples with stark fiscal realities, putting off important decisions on tax and spending until next year.
“The world’s a highly uncertain place,” the chancellor said, in a video released before the budget. “Conflicts abroad are pushing up energy prices, and the cost of living here at home – piling pressure on the families, on businesses and on our public finances.”
Healey insisted the government would move to ease the cost of living “responsibly” by sticking to Labour’s self-imposed fiscal rules, as he attempts to reassure the markets that his plans for longer-term reform will make Britain “more resilient” from global shocks.
The chancellor has limited scope for big giveaways because of the stretched public finances, made worse by international market turmoil caused by the Iran conflict, but changes aimed at easing the cost of living are set to feature heavily.
In his pre-budget address, he added: “This budget is about getting through this difficult moment. But it’s also about putting Britain on a future path, a better future path.”
Healey is expected to offer temporary support for poorer families before a steep rise in typical energy bills in January; while pledging energy market reforms aimed at bringing down bills for all households in the longer term.
Andy Burnham recently told MPs he was keen to see the gas standing charge – a fixed daily levy on all users – abolished. The move would bring down bills for consumers who use less energy, and the cost would be picked up by those who use more.
Industry experts fear further investment in hydrogen and carbon capture is likely to bear the brunt of efforts to rein in extra spending, in a blow to the UK’s net zero targets.
As part of a series of “everyday fixes”, the chancellor is expected to end the carers’ allowance cliff edge, which has penalised unpaid carers for going over their earnings limit, even by as little as a few pence a week. Healey is also expected to cancel January’s planned increase in fuel duty.
The government has been under pressure to use the budget to set out a clear path for defence spending to hit 3% of national income by 2030 – a target Healey claimed to be committed to when he resigned as defence secretary earlier this year.
But while he is expected to confirm more investment in defence industries – described as a “downpayment” on hitting the target – Healey is expected to wait until next year’s spending review to confirm the timetable.
The budget will also set out a “roadmap” to devolving more tax revenues to local leaders in a significant shift towards moving spending power away from Whitehall to the regions and nations of the UK.
But the detail of Burnham’s devolution agenda in areas such as skills and employment support is not expected until the government publishes a white paper in the weeks ahead.
Cutting energy prices has the added benefit of bringing down inflation, helping to ease pressure on the Bank of England to raise interest rates. Markets are now expecting the Bank to hike rates four times, to 4.75%, over the next 12 months.
Healey is also expected to take action to offset part of the hit to the public finances from higher interest rates on government borrowing – the result of rising inflation and turmoil in global bond markets.
The government had to pay the highest yield, or interest rate, on new five-year bonds since 2008 on Tuesday, above 5%.
City analysts say bond market investors will be watching the budget closely – though the upward move in UK yields, or interest rates, have echoed those seen in other major economies.
The UK’s economy has proved more resilient than expected in the face of the Iran conflict but recent data has pointed to a deteriorating outlook.
At a cabinet meeting last week, Healey told ministers that rising inflation caused by the conflict, which hit an in-year high of 3.5% last month, was the political backdrop to the budget.
Consumer confidence has fallen at the fastest rate since Brexit; while the number of businesses in financial distress has hit its highest level in more than two decades, according to data published by consultancy BTG on Thursday, with hospitality and construction hardest hit.
Healey struck an optimistic note, however, saying: “Britain’s economy is showing real signs of resilience: investment’s up, productivity is growing and we had the joint fastest growth in the G7 in the first half of this year.”
Healey will announce plans to increase the minimum wage by nearly 4% but slow the rise for younger people under the age of 21 after warnings that they are being priced out of jobs but prompting accusations that Labour had broken a manifesto pledge.
He is also expected to protect pensioners and those saving for their retirement by shielding nearly one million people from paying income tax and is preparing to make the government’s revived Help to Buy scheme more generous, in a boost to middle-earners.
To help offset the damage inflicted on the public finances by war in the Middle East, Healey is poised to raise taxes for Britain’s banks, potentially reversing cuts to the bank surcharge made by Jeremy Hunt, which would raise upwards of £2bn a year. Online retailers will be responsible for collecting tax owed by firms selling on their platforms.
The Tories said the chancellor was set to “shy away” from the difficult decisions, including bringing down the welfare bill, which the prime minister has said he does not want to do through “crude cuts”.
The shadow chief secretary to the Treasury, Richard Fuller, said: “Britain’s public finances are on a cliff edge. A ‘do-nothing’ budget will not solve the problems staring us in the face: a spiralling welfare bill, a crippling tax burden, mounting debt and rising global threats.”
The Lib Dems warned against a “steady as she goes” budget. Their deputy leader, Daisy Cooper, said: “Families are being squeezed from all sides, businesses face mounting costs and for many it feels like even the basic joys in life have become unaffordable.”

title: Wahl in Israel: "König Bibi" polarisiert - setzt er sich noch mal durch?
content_c:
Israel wählt neues Parlament "König Bibi" polarisiert - setzt er sich noch mal durch?
Benjamin Netanjahu hat Israel länger regiert als jeder andere Politiker vor ihm. Heute entscheiden die Wähler, ob eine weitere Amtszeit dazukommt. Es ist eine Abstimmung über einen Premier, der im Land wie kein Zweiter polarisiert.
Wer in diesen Tagen mit den Menschen in den Fußgängerzonen von Jerusalem oder Tel Aviv über die Wahl zur Knesset spricht, erlebt ein zutiefst zerrissenes Land. Die Gräben verlaufen quer durch Familien, Freundeskreise und die gesamte Gesellschaft. Und im Epizentrum dieser Zerrissenheit steht nun schon seit Jahren unverändert ein einziger Name: Benjamin Netanjahu.
Für seine treuen Anhänger, das Establishment der Likud-Partei und die religiös-nationale Rechte, ist er schlicht "König Bibi", der unersetzbare Führer und der verlässliche Beschützer des jüdischen Volkes. Seine Kritiker dagegen sehen in ihm einen rücksichtslosen, vom puren Selbsterhalt getriebenen Machtpolitiker. Einen Mann, dem das eigene politische Überleben und der Verbleib im Amt längst wichtiger seien als das Wohl und die demokratische Stabilität des Staates.
Sein zentrales Versprechen: Sicherheit
Netanjahus politische DNA ist seit Beginn seiner Karriere untrennbar mit einem zentralen Versprechen verknüpft: Sicherheit. Er inszeniert sich meisterhaft als der einzige Führer Israels, der den Mut und die strategische Härte besitzt, sich den existenziellen Bedrohungen in der Region und, wenn nötig, auch der gesamten Weltöffentlichkeit entgegenzustellen.
Wie tief dieses Selbstverständnis sitzt, demonstrierte der Premier erst vor wenigen Wochen vor den Vereinten Nationen in New York. Gleich zu Beginn seiner Rede - Dutzende Diplomaten hatten kurz zuvor den Saal verlassen - legte er die diplomatische Etikette demonstrativ beiseite und rief den Delegierten im Saal entgegen: "Sollte es hier noch weitere moralische Feiglinge geben, die den Raum noch nicht verlassen haben, so mögen sie dies bitte jetzt tun. Danke."
Es ist genau diese kompromisslose, oft konfrontative Rhetorik, die bei einem großen Teil der israelischen Bevölkerung verfängt. In einer Region, die von permanenten geopolitischen Erschütterungen geprägt ist, sehnen sich Millionen von Israelis nach einer starken Hand.
Die Wählerbasis fordert Härte
Nach den kollektiven Traumata der vergangenen Jahre - insbesondere nach den verheerenden Terrorangriffen der Hamas vom 7. Oktober 2023 - positioniert sich Netanjahu umso vehementer als das unerschütterliche Bollwerk gegen Israels Feinde.
Er inszeniert sich als ein Führer, der in der Krise keine Schwäche zeigt und den erbitterten Kampf an mehreren Fronten als historischen Auftrag versteht. "Unser Volk ist stark. Die Israelis sind eine Nation von Löwen mit unbegrenzter Entschlossenheit, unser Land zu verteidigen und unsere Zukunft zu sichern", betont Netanjahu immer wieder in seinen martialischen Ansprachen an die Nation:
                
                
                Das jüdische Volk ist immer wieder aus der Asche auferstanden. Aber als wir den Staat Israel und die Armee Israels gründeten, gelobten wir: Nie wieder. Nie wieder würden wir unseren Feinden schutzlos ausgeliefert sein.
Für die rechtskonservative Wählerbasis ist "Bibi" der einzige Politiker, der bereit ist, militärische Operationen auch gegen internationalen Druck und diplomatische Warnungen westlicher Verbündeter zu Ende zu bringen.
Seine Unterstützer rechnen ihm das konsequente Vorgehen der vergangenen Monate hoch an: die Zerschlagung der Infrastruktur der Hisbollah im Südlibanon, das Zurückdrängen der Hamas im Gazastreifen und die direkten Militärschläge gegen das Regime und dessen Stellvertreter in Teheran. In ihren Augen führt Netanjahu einen existenziellen Verteidigungskampf, bei dem Kompromisse Lebensgefahr bedeuten.
Massendemonstrationen gegen Justizumbau
Für die Opposition und Hunderttausende Israelis, die seit Monaten regelmäßig auf die Straßen gehen, ist diese Inszenierung als starker Landesvater jedoch nur eine Fassade. Sie blicken mit Entsetzen auf die tiefen innenpolitischen Verwerfungen, die Netanjahus Regierungszeit dem Land eingebrockt hat.
Der massivste gesellschaftliche Protest in der Geschichte des Staates entzündete sich an der von seiner Koalition vorangetriebenen, höchst umstrittenen Justizreform. Kritiker, Juristen und weite Teile der High-Tech- und Militärelite werfen Netanjahu vor, die Unabhängigkeit der Gerichte gezielt zu beschneiden und damit Demokratie und Rechtsstaatlichkeit in Israel systematisch auszuhebeln.
Hinzu kommen die seit Jahren schwelenden Korruptionsprozesse wegen Betrugs, Untreue und Bestechlichkeit, die den Premierminister persönlich schwer belasten. Das Thema schlägt internationale Wellen: Sogar sein enger politischer Verbündeter, US-Präsident Donald Trump, schaltete sich ein und forderte während einer Rede vor der Knesset öffentlich eine Begnadigung des israelischen Regierungschefs.
Der Vorwurf: "Purer Selbsterhalt"
Für ehemalige Weggefährten wie Moshe Yaalon, den einstigen israelischen Verteidigungsminister, hat sich Netanjahus Triebfeder im Laufe der Jahrzehnte fundamental verändert. Er sieht im Premier keinen Staatsmann mehr, der vom klassischen zionistischen Ideal geleitet wird, sondern einen Politiker im permanenten Überlebensmodus.
"Er will an der Macht festhalten", kritisiert Yaalon scharf. "Wer also behauptet, er habe keine Strategie, der irrt: Er hat sehr wohl eine Strategie, doch diese hat nichts mit Außenbeziehungen, unserer Sicherheit oder den Interessen des Staates Israel zu tun. Es geht ihm einzig darum, aus persönlichen Interessen an der Macht zu bleiben."
Ähnlich umstritten wie Benjamin Netanjahu ist seine Ehefrau Sara. Kritiker schreiben ihr einen großen Einfluss auf seine Personalpolitik zu.
Rechtsextreme Allianzen und der Einfluss im Hintergrund
Um dieses Überleben und seine Regierungsmehrheiten zu sichern, ging Netanjahu in den vergangenen Jahren Allianzen ein, die vor Kurzem noch als politisch undenkbar galten. Er formte Koalitionen mit ultranationalistischen, rechtsextremen und streng orthodoxen Kräften.
Kritiker monieren, dass diese Partner Zugeständnisse erpressen, die das ohnehin fragile gesellschaftliche Gefüge zwischen säkularen und religiösen Israelis sowie der arabischen Minderheit bis aufs Äußerste strapazieren.
Wie sehr Netanjahus Politik und Machtapparat nicht nur von ideologischen, sondern auch von hochgradig privaten Dynamiken bestimmt werden, enthüllen Berichte von Insidern aus dem engsten Zirkel der Macht. Nir Hefetz, Netanjahus langjähriger Sprecher und Vertrauter, beschreibt den außergewöhnlich großen Einfluss, den Ehefrau Sara Netanjahu im Hintergrund ausübt.
"Keine zentrale Personalentscheidung im Büro des Premierministers kommt ohne Saras Zustimmung zustande", berichtet Hefetz aus der Innensicht. "Ich würde sogar sagen, sie hat das absolute - und ich meine wirklich 'absolute', also uneingeschränkte - Monopol darauf, zu entscheiden, ob man jemandem vertrauen kann oder nicht."
Das Bild, das Insider zeichnen, zeigt ein System, in dem Loyalität zum Ehepaar Netanjahu über der fachlichen Eignung für Staatsämter steht.
Abstimmung auch über Netanjahus Erbe
In den Wahllokalen geht es heute für die Menschen in Israel um weit mehr als um die klassischen Parteiprogramme, Wirtschaftsfragen oder Sozialpolitik. Es ist eine Schicksalswahl und ein Referendum über ein zutiefst umstrittenes politisches Erbe.
Netanjahu hat das Land über Generationen geprägt wie kein Zweiter. Am Wahltag entscheidet sich, welchen Weg Israel einschlägt: Folgt die Mehrheit dem Narrativ des "Königs Bibi", dem unnachgiebigen Strategen in Zeiten des Krieges? Oder setzt sich die Erschöpfung einer Gesellschaft durch, die in ihm den großen Spalter sieht, der das Land an den Rand des demokratischen Abgrunds geführt hat? Die Antwort darauf wird die Zukunft des Nahen Ostens maßgeblich mitbestimmen.
Die Wahllokale sind zwischen 7.00 Uhr und 22.00 Uhr Ortszeit geöffnet (6.00 Uhr und 21.00 Uhr MEZ). Unmittelbar nach Schließung der Wahllokale veröffentlichen die israelischen Fernsehsender Prognosen auf Grundlage von Nachwahlbefragungen, die erste Hinweise auf den Wahlausgang geben könnten. Sollte kein Bündnis eine deutliche parlamentarische Mehrheit erreichen, könnte es jedoch dauern, bis sich ein klares Bild abzeichnet.
Die Mandate werden nach dem Verhältniswahlrecht über landesweite Parteilisten vergeben. Dabei müssen die Parteien eine Sperrklausel von 3,25 Prozent der abgegebenen Stimmen überwinden. Etwa ein Dutzend Parteien könnte diese Hürde nehmen. Die endgültige Auszählung und die Sitzverteilung dauern entsprechend lange. Das vorläufige Ergebnis wird für den 30. Oktober erwartet. Das amtliche Endergebnis wird eine Woche nach der Wahl, am 4. November, veröffentlicht.
Anschließend beauftragt der israelische Präsident jenen Kandidaten mit der Regierungsbildung, dem die besten Chancen eingeräumt werden. Dieser hat zunächst vier Wochen Zeit, eine Koalition zu schmieden.

title: Не кажіть “хворіти грипом”: філологиня розповіла, як правильно українською і назвала поширені помилки
content_c:
Не кажіть “хворіти грипом”: філологиня розповіла, як правильно українською і назвала поширені помилки
Філологиня пояснила, як правильно відмінювати складні іменники та вживати прийменники у повсякденному мовленні.
Українська мовознавиця розвіяла поширені міфи та помилки, які українці часто допускають у щоденному спілкуванні.
Експертка Оксана у відео на Facebook розібрала найскладніші випадки правопису та керування слів, які викликають найбільше суперечок.
Зокрема, фахівчиня пояснила правильне вживання дієслова «хворіти». За її словами, у цьому разі завжди слід використовувати прийменник «на», тож правильно говорити: «хворіти на грип» чи «хворіти на ангіну».
Окрему увагу мовознавиця приділила закінченням іменників у родовому відмінку множини. Зокрема, у питанні «огляду готелів» слід обирати форму «готелів», оскільки слово належить до чоловічого роду, для якого характерне закінчення «-ів», тоді як для жіночого властиве «-ей».
Також експертка нагадала про правильне відмінювання середнього роду на прикладі слова «пальто». Багато хто помилково не змінює його за відмінками, однак правильно казати у родовому відмінку «немає пальта». Це ж правило стосується й інших подібних слів, таких як «ситро», «віче», «вино» чи «ложе», які також підлягають відмінюванню.
Щодо граматичних форм власних назв, мовознавиця Оксана звернула увагу на правильне відмінювання прізвищ. Коли йдеться про пам’ятник, поставлений конкретній людині на її честь, у давальному відмінку слід відповідати на питання «кому?» — Шевченку, Лесі Українці чи Квітці-Основ’яненку, адже йдеться не про власне майно діяча, а про пам’ять про нього.
Насамкінець фахівчиня зачепила тему вживання дієслова «дивуватися» із займенниками. За її словами, у цьому випадку нормативними є одразу два варіанти, тому цілком правильно казати як «дивуватися із тебе», так і «дивуватися тобі».
Зауважимо, в українській мові форми «мати» і «матір» є нормативними, а їхній вибір залежить від відмінка та значення в реченні. «Мати» — це називний відмінок, тоді як «матір» найчастіше вживають у знахідному, тому механічно замінювати одне слово іншим не можна.
description: Філологиня пояснила, як правильно відмінювати складні іменники та вживати прийменники у повсякденному мовленні.
content:
Не кажіть “хворіти грипом”: філологиня розповіла, як правильно українською і назвала поширені помилки
Філологиня пояснила, як правильно відмінювати складні іменники та вживати прийменники у повсякденному мовленні.
Українська мовознавиця розвіяла поширені міфи та помилки, які українці часто допускають у щоденному спілкуванні.
Експертка Оксана у відео на Facebook розібрала найскладніші випадки правопису та керування слів, які викликають найбільше суперечок.
Зокрема, фахівчиня пояснила правильне вживання дієслова «хворіти». За її словами, у цьому разі завжди слід використовувати прийменник «на», тож правильно говорити: «хворіти на грип» чи «хворіти на ангіну».
Окрему увагу мовознавиця приділила закінченням іменників у родовому відмінку множини. Зокрема, у питанні «огляду готелів» слід обирати форму «готелів», оскільки слово належить до чоловічого роду, для якого характерне закінчення «-ів», тоді як для жіночого властиве «-ей».
Також експертка нагадала про правильне відмінювання середнього роду на прикладі слова «пальто». Багато хто помилково не змінює його за відмінками, однак правильно казати у родовому відмінку «немає пальта». Це ж правило стосується й інших подібних слів, таких як «ситро», «віче», «вино» чи «ложе», які також підлягають відмінюванню.
Щодо граматичних форм власних назв, мовознавиця Оксана звернула увагу на правильне відмінювання прізвищ. Коли йдеться про пам’ятник, поставлений конкретній людині на її честь, у давальному відмінку слід відповідати на питання «кому?» — Шевченку, Лесі Українці чи Квітці-Основ’яненку, адже йдеться не про власне майно діяча, а про пам’ять про нього.
Насамкінець фахівчиня зачепила тему вживання дієслова «дивуватися» із займенниками. За її словами, у цьому випадку нормативними є одразу два варіанти, тому цілком правильно казати як «дивуватися із тебе», так і «дивуватися тобі».
Зауважимо, в українській мові форми «мати» і «матір» є нормативними, а їхній вибір залежить від відмінка та значення в реченні. «Мати» — це називний відмінок, тоді як «матір» найчастіше вживають у знахідному, тому механічно замінювати одне слово іншим не можна.

title: Зеленский отметил операции «Велес» и «Вивальди»: что известно об успехах ВСУ
content_c:
Президент Владимир Зеленский заслушал доклады об успешных операциях ВСУ на фронте. Среди них он отметил операцию «Велес», которую назвал «продуманной и технологичной».
По словам президента, россияне пытались использовать подземные газовые трубы, чтобы продвигаться мимо позиций ВСУ, однако потерпели поражение. Украинские военные использовали эти подземные коммуникации против самих оккупантов.
«Операция “Велес” от “Хартии” укрепляет наши позиции и демонстрирует россиянам, что и под Купянском у них нет того результата, который им определило их политическое руководство», — отметил Зеленский.
Он также отметил успехи операции ДШВ, в ходе которой было освобождено 800 квадратных километров территории. В ходе операции «Вивальди» освободили ещё более 200 квадратных километров — именно в тех районах, где россияне проводили наибольшее количество штурмов.
Зеленский добавил, что с 2022 года позиции Украины на фронте остаются самыми сильными.
В то же время президент сообщил о нехватке ракет для защиты от российской баллистики и задержках с поставками пакетов противовоздушной обороны. Это происходит на фоне того, что только с 14 октября оккупанты запустили по Киеву и области более 100 баллистических ракет.
«В эти дни мы стараемся сделать всё возможное, чтобы появились новые пакеты поддержки. Также продолжается координация с партнёрами, чтобы велась дипломатия, чтобы состоялись встречи, причём как можно скорее. В ноябре мы ожидаем трехсторонний формат: украинские, американские и российские представители. Важно, чтобы Европа также участвовала во всех дипломатических инициативах. Украина всегда настаивает на том, что Европа должна присутствовать, должна участвовать в принятии решений. Причем это касается всех в Европе. И чтобы никто не остался в стороне от этих процессов», — подытожил Зеленский.
Ранее ZN.UA сообщало, что во время ночной атаки 22 октября Россия применила против Киева 21 баллистическую ракету. В результате ударов были повреждены жилые дома, энергетические объекты и транспортная инфраструктура, в частности метро и Южный мост.
description: Президент рассказал об использовании подземных газопроводов против российских войск и освобождении территорий на фронте.

title: Тристоронні перемовини в ОАЕ між Україною, США та РФ попередньо заплановані на 4 листопада, повідомив Туск
content_c:
Прем'єр-міністр Польщі Дональд Туск повідомив, що переговори в Абу-Дабі (ОАЕ) між Україною, РФ та США на рівні команд попередньо заплановані на 4 листопада поточного року.
Як повідомляє The Guardian, про це очільник польського уряду повідомив, коментуючи телефонну розмову президента Фінляндії Александера Стубба та прем'єр-міністра Норвегії Йонаса Ґара Стьоре з Володимиром Путіним. За його словами, дзвінок відбувся після "консультацій, зокрема, зі мною, але насамперед із президентом Зеленським та американською стороною… щодо того, що європейським політикам було б корисно налагодити робочі контакти з огляду на заплановані переговори про перемир'я, які можуть відбутися в Абу-Дабі".
Туск зазначив, що Стубб проінформував його після телефонної розмови, що "обидві сторони дотрималися своїх позицій", і що "під час розмови європейська сторона відчувала дуже стриманий оптимізм" щодо шансів досягти прогресу в Абу-Дабі.
Прем'єр Польщі заявив, що ставиться до взаємодії з РФ "дуже обережно" і закликав Стубба та Стьоре бути "пильними" під час переговорів із Путіним, оскільки "порядок денний та інтереси Росії чітко визначені, і не варто плекати жодних ілюзій щодо досягнення угоди".
Він зазначив, що Стубб і Стьоре повідомили Путіну, що безпека північного та східного флангів НАТО "не підлягають обговоренню".
Очільник уряду також наголосив, що, незважаючи на відновлення діалогу, "нічого не змінюється" у "повній підтримці України" з боку Європи, а також у колективних поглядах на архітектуру безпеки та гарантії безпеки для України.
"Ми не повинні мати жодних ілюзій; зрозуміло, у що грає російська сторона, але я залишатимуся в постійному контакті з усіма, хто має добру волю та віру в те, що угода можлива – або, принаймні, перемир'я до настання зими", – сказав Туск, підсумовуючи результати перемовин.
Як повідомлялося, Зеленський обговорив із Стуббом і Стьоре їх розмову з Путіним та подякував їм за "активність на підтримку нашої дипломатії та спільних з усіма партнерами мирних зусиль". За словами президента України, президент Фінляндії і прем'єр Норвегії сказали російському керівнику про те, що потрібні реальні деескалаційні кроки щодо енергетики та інфраструктури України. Також у розмові вони обговорили підготовку тристоронньої зустрічі Україна-США-РФ, яка запланована на листопад в Абу-Дабі (ОАЕ) на рівні команд.

title: 'I would do it again' - Kaepernick reflects on price of protest, 10 years on
content_c:
"I knew the protest could potentially cost me my career...I would absolutely do it again."
Ten years on from making the gesture that catapulted him to iconic status, but which he believes led to his exile from the sport he loved, Colin Kaepernick insists he has no regrets.
It was September 2016 when NFL star Kaepernick knelt during the US national anthem before a match as a peaceful protest against racial injustice and police brutality.
It proved both inspirational and divisive.
In his first interview with BBC Sport, Kaepernick reflects on his journey; his pride at seeing England footballers take the knee, athlete activism, the relationship between sport and politics, and the price he paid for being a figurehead for the civil rights movement.
The former quarterback says he decided to protest despite suspecting it could risk his career.
"History shows us…that is a reality for athletes", he says.
"We also see this in broader movements, going well beyond costing someone their career, and costing people their lives. We see Malcolm X assassinated, we see MLK [Martin Luther King] assassinated, so the consequences are real."
Having initially sat to raise awareness of the plight of black people in the US, Kaepernick first knelt during the Star-Spangled Banner before his San Francisco 49ers team played a pre-season game. It was an act he would repeat before 11 regular-season contests that year.
At the time, he said he could not stand up for - and show pride in - a flag "for a country that oppresses black people and people of colour", adding: "This is bigger than football and it would be selfish on my part to look the other way."
His stance against racial inequality was seen as heroic by many, inspiring other NFL players to follow suit. But there was also condemnation from those who said it was disrespectful to the military.
Those dissenting voices included Donald Trump - then a presidential candidate.
Trump described the act as "a terrible thing" and unpatriotic. He even suggested Kaepernick should find another country to live in, adding players who refused to stand for the national anthem should be fired.
The NFL said it would fine teams whose players did not stand.
Kaepernick opted out of his contract with the 49ers in March 2017, though the club's management later said he would have been released regardless.
Despite leading the 49ers to the 2013 Super Bowl, and throwing 16 touchdowns in his final season, one of the most talented quarterbacks in the sport never found a new team.
Speaking from New York, Kaepernick says he anticipated the reaction to taking the knee. "What I couldn't have predicted was the people who would show up for me in significant ways, and also the people who worked against me and against the movement," he adds.
Kaepernick eventually filed a grievance against NFL team owners, who he believed had conspired not to hire him because of his protests, reaching a financial settlement in 2019.
That year, the NFL arranged a private workout for Kaepernick, but he chose not to attend, instead holding his own session elsewhere to allow media to be present. Hopes of a comeback never materialised.
The NFL later admitted it was "wrong for not listening to players earlier", and encouraged "all to speak out and peacefully protest".
Colin Kaepernick speaks to BBC's Dan Roan
Available now
Former NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick gives his first interview with BBC Sport, 10 years on from making the gesture that catapulted him to iconic status
'Humbling to see England players take knee'
Following the murder of George Floyd while in police custody in Minneapolis in 2020, taking the knee became a feature of Black Lives Matter protests, and widespread across sport.
England's men's and women's football teams were among those to follow suit.
"That was a surprising moment for me," says Kaepernick.
"I did think about the protest going beyond the US and how that may show up in other countries. To be able to see the national teams going out and protesting, it was humbling. I was happy that they were doing it.
"I also know there's still a lot of work to be done within racism in the UK and more broadly. And this is a global challenge that we are collectively fighting against.
"I was very excited to be able to see players actively calling that out, and willing to begin taking action towards addressing it."
Despite keeping a relatively low profile for most of the past decade, Kaepernick remains a standard-bearer for the civil rights movement.
But while surveys suggest the vast majority of professional athletes intend to use their social media channels to raise awareness about racial injustice, external, he accepts the momentum behind athlete activism seems to have slowed in recent years.
It was notable that several players across five clubs chose to remain standing when Premier League players took the knee as part of October's No Room for Racism campaign.
Anti-discrimination campaign group Kick It Out told BBC Sport the gesture "still has value in raising awareness of the structural inequalities that exist in football and society", but added it could "understand the reasons players might become frustrated with the pace of change".
Reports of discrimination received by the charity more than doubled in the past five years, reaching record levels last season.
"I think we're in a moment that demands protests more than ever," says Kaepernick.
"Why I think protests are not as loud right now [is] because of the concerted efforts that have been taken by organisations like the NFL, like the Trump administration, and corporate entities following along and capitulating in that process.
"While those things are happening, I think the reality of the state of the US, and more broadly the world, demands that we show up in a more significant way."
'Politics inherently part of sports'
Kaepernick is all too familiar with how polarising it can be to take a political stand in sport.
Opponents of taking the knee have claimed it is a political and divisive statement, and that rather than demonstrating backing for the Black Lives Matter movement, it has shown support for the organisation of the same name.
In 2018, critics encouraged people to destroy Nike goods after the sportswear giant used Kaepernick as the face of an advertising campaign featuring the caption 'Believe in something. Even if it means sacrificing everything.'
So what does he say to those who argue that sport and politics should be kept apart?
"They ring hollow and feel very hypocritical, because politics is inherently part of sports," he says.
"We see within [American] football, we see taxpayers funding NFL stadiums. We see our NFL owners going out and supporting political candidates... so to try to position this as if sports aren't political, in many ways feels just laughable to me, and disconnected.
"Now, where the question comes in for people is: 'We don't want the athletes to be political. Everything around them can be political, but the athletes themselves, we don't want them to have a voice in the politics, because that interrupts our entertainment and our ability to disconnect.' For me, that's where society has a challenge with it."
Having encountered significant opposition from high-profile athletes during his first term, Trump seems to have encountered less challenge from the world of sport during his second, notably becoming the first sitting US president to attend the Super Bowl.
He has also appeared at golf's Ryder Cup, and the finals of football's Club World Cup and World Cup, though he was also booed when attending the NBA Finals in New York in June.
"It ties into the conversation of 'are sports political?' when he is going out and actively trying to use them to gain favour and popularity", says Kaepernick, adding that Fifa's controversial decision to award the US President its inaugural 'Peace Prize' last year was "regrettable".
"The part that I think is great to see is when he's showing up to these events and getting booed by the crowd, which speaks to the political environment that he's created, that the majority of the country does not agree with…when it comes to sports, people need to continue to respond accordingly."
'We have a lot of work to do'
Now 38, Kaepernick has published a memoir titled The Perilous Fight, detailing his childhood in California having been adopted by a white family, encountering racism, and his education and evolution. "People saw the moment. But they didn't see the years that made it possible", he says. "The questions about who I was; the injustices I could no longer ignore; the voices of those who came before me that I carried into that stadium...When I took a knee, it wasn't a sudden act. It was the result of years of becoming."
So how did he find the process of reliving that journey?
"Are there moments that are challenging going back to? Yes. But I hope that insight helps other people navigate situations...that helps them move forward or helps them to go accomplish things."
Kaepernick also supports community organisations via his Know Your Rights education campaign, is a philanthropist, and has written a number of children's books.
Even now, he maintains the fitness regime he had during his time at the 49ers, just in case an unlikely opportunity to resume his NFL career arises.
Kaepernick may not have thrown a ball in anger for almost a decade, but he is widely regarded as one of the most significant athletes in modern history.
The way he used his platform to promote change has been compared to legendary boxer Muhammad Ali's support of the anti-war movement, and US athletes Tommie Smith and John Carlos giving the Black Power Salute at the 1968 Olympics.
"To even be in the same conversation with the likes of [them], is extremely humbling," he says. "But more importantly, I just try to stay focused on the work.
"What can we do to help people? And how do we collectively move forward as a society? And, ultimately, how we build a society that works for everybody. That feels like a very simple principle that has been lost.
"I know in the US specifically, we have a lot of work to do there. I hope we begin taking the steps to get back to a place where we are actually addressing people's needs. And create a society that is equitable for everyone."
description: In his first interview with BBC Sport since taking the knee for the first time, Colin Kaepernick reflects on his journey.
content:
"I knew the protest could potentially cost me my career...I would absolutely do it again."
Ten years on from making the gesture that catapulted him to iconic status, but which he believes led to his exile from the sport he loved, Colin Kaepernick insists he has no regrets.
It was September 2016 when NFL star Kaepernick knelt during the US national anthem before a match as a peaceful protest against racial injustice and police brutality.
It proved both inspirational and divisive.
In his first interview with BBC Sport, Kaepernick reflects on his journey; his pride at seeing England footballers take the knee, athlete activism, the relationship between sport and politics, and the price he paid for being a figurehead for the civil rights movement.
The former quarterback says he decided to protest despite suspecting it could risk his career.
"History shows us…that is a reality for athletes", he says.
"We also see this in broader movements, going well beyond costing someone their career, and costing people their lives. We see Malcolm X assassinated, we see MLK [Martin Luther King] assassinated, so the consequences are real."
Having initially sat to raise awareness of the plight of black people in the US, Kaepernick first knelt during the Star-Spangled Banner before his San Francisco 49ers team played a pre-season game. It was an act he would repeat before 11 regular-season contests that year.
At the time, he said he could not stand up for - and show pride in - a flag "for a country that oppresses black people and people of colour", adding: "This is bigger than football and it would be selfish on my part to look the other way."
His stance against racial inequality was seen as heroic by many, inspiring other NFL players to follow suit. But there was also condemnation from those who said it was disrespectful to the military.
Those dissenting voices included Donald Trump - then a presidential candidate.
Trump described the act as "a terrible thing" and unpatriotic. He even suggested Kaepernick should find another country to live in, adding players who refused to stand for the national anthem should be fired.
The NFL said it would fine teams whose players did not stand.
Kaepernick opted out of his contract with the 49ers in March 2017, though the club's management later said he would have been released regardless.
Despite leading the 49ers to the 2013 Super Bowl, and throwing 16 touchdowns in his final season, one of the most talented quarterbacks in the sport never found a new team.

Kaepernick eventually filed a grievance against NFL team owners, who he believed had conspired not to hire him because of his protests, reaching a financial settlement in 2019.
That year, the NFL arranged a private workout for Kaepernick, but he chose not to attend, instead holding his own session elsewhere to allow media to be present. Hopes of a comeback never materialised.
The NFL later admitted it was "wrong for not listening to players earlier", and encouraged "all to speak out and peacefully protest".

title: AI bots flooded 2023 UK government consultation on disposable vapes ban
content_c:
AI bots flooded a government consultation with tens of thousands of fake responses in a failed attempt to stop the UK’s ban on disposable vapes.
Three-quarters of all the responses to the 2023 consultation on the tobacco and vapes bill were machine-generated, in what is thought to be the first coordinated attempt to use AI to derail health policymaking in the UK.
The attempt to manipulate the outcome of the consultation was disclosed on Tuesday in research published in the journal Tobacco Control by the health policy experts Dr Nason Maani, from the University of Edinburgh, and Prof Anna Gilmore, of the University of Bath.
The Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) used bot-detection methods to identify that 90,835 of the 118,756 responses it received, 76%, were submitted by bots.
All but two of those 90,835 automated responses answered the same question in the “smoke free generation” consultation, in which they opposed Rishi Sunak’s Conservative government’s plan to ban disposable vapes. The submissions were “often duplicated many times and sent at high frequency from a small number of IP addresses”, the DHSC said.
The bombardment “appears to be the first documented instance of large-scale automated interference in a formal public health policy consultation”, the researchers said.
Maani added that while this attempt was identified, “the threat is that future campaigns become harder to catch, and what we can’t catch, we don’t know about. Such campaigns are a threat because they raise the possibility of a handful of powerful interests looking like a mass movement.”
The DHSC excluded the 90,835 automated responses from its decision-making. Keir Starmer’s Labour government inherited the tobacco and vapes bill in 2024 and passed it into law, including the ban on businesses selling or supplying disposable vapes.
Caroline Cerny, the deputy chief executive of Action on Smoking and Health, said: “Evidence that AI bots have been used to swamp a Department of Health consultation is deeply concerning.
“Given the tobacco industry’s history of seeking to undermine public health regulation, we need to be alert to the risk that technological advances can be used to further commercial interests around health policy and put safeguards in place.
“Decisions that affect public health must be based on sound evidence and expertise, not manipulated response numbers.”
Azzurra Moores, the associate director for information ecosystems at the thinktank Demos, described the attempt to derail the ban as “pretty alarming”.
“Public consultations are one of the main ways government opens up its decision-making, so any interference with them is a serious concern,” she said. “These findings are pretty alarming: if a consultation can be swamped like this, it stops telling policymakers what the public actually thinks and undermines trust in the process.
“This is a problem without easy answers. Every barrier that keeps bots out also makes it harder for real people to take part, and AI makes fake responses far harder to spot. Interference can adapt faster than departments can update their checks. Better screening and more transparency will help, but there’s no single fix.”
The DHSC said its “robust controls” identified the attempt to influence the consultation.
A spokesperson said: “We always have robust controls in place to prevent the manipulation of our public consultations, and those controls worked effectively in this case.
“As a result, the fake responses were removed, and the consultation helped inform the landmark action we are taking to create a smoke-free generation.
“We will remain alert to interference of this kind in future consultation processes, and we will not be deterred from doing what is necessary to promote healthier living.”

title: Juli Zeh: Schriftstellerin hört offenbar als Verfassungsrichterin auf
content_c:
Medienbericht Juli Zeh hört offenbar als Verfassungsrichterin auf
Die meisten Menschen kennen Juli Zeh als Autorin von Erfolgsromanen wie »Unterleuten«. Aber: Die 52-Jährige ist gelernte Juristin und als solche auch immer noch tätig. Künftig jedoch womöglich deutlich seltener: Zeh hat einem Bericht zufolge ihre Entlassung als ehrenamtliche Verfassungsrichterin beantragt.
Wie die »Märkische Allgemeine Zeitung« schreibt, habe Julia Barbara Finck, wie sie bürgerlich heißt, die Brandenburger Landtagspräsidentin Ulrike Liedtke (SPD) via Brief um die Amtsaufgabe gebeten. Eigentlich würde ihre reguläre zehnjährige Amtszeit als Verfassungsrichterin in Potsdam erst 2029 enden.
Hohe Arbeitsbelastung als Schriftstellerin
Zur Begründung gab Zeh dem Bericht zufolge ihre beruflichen Verpflichtungen als Schriftstellerin und die damit verbundene hohe Arbeitsbelastung an. Die Autorin tourt derzeit mit ihrem neuen Roman »Pony Show« durch Deutschland. (Lesen Sie hier die SPIEGEL-Rezension des Buchs )
Auf Anfrage der Zeitung, die zum Redaktionsnetzwerk Deutschland gehört, äußerten sich zunächst weder Zeh selbst noch der Landtag zu dem Schritt. Zeh bedauerte laut »MAZ« in dem Schreiben zugleich aber ihre Entscheidung. Die Tätigkeit am Gericht habe sie stets als besondere Ehre und Verantwortung empfunden, heißt es demnach.
Prüfung von Gesetzen und Regeln von Streitigkeiten
Zeh war im Dezember 2018 auf Vorschlag der SPD mit einer Zweidrittelmehrheit vom Landtag gewählt und Ende Januar 2019 als Verfassungsrichterin vereidigt worden.
Als solche ist Zeh mit ihren Kolleginnen und Kollegen unter anderem für die Prüfung von Gesetzen, sowie Verfassungsbeschwerden und Streitigkeiten zwischen staatlichen Organen zuständig. Das Gericht setzt sich aus neun Mitgliedern zusammen – darunter Berufsrichterinnen und -richter, Menschen mit der Befähigung zum Richteramt oder Diplomjuristen und auch Laien.
Ende 2022 wurde Zeh von SPIEGEL-Autor und -Moderator Markus Feldenkirchen zum »Spitzengespräch« eingeladen. Beide redeten unter anderem über den Krieg Russlands gegen die Ukraine. »Hinterher sagten viele, ich hätte ihr keine Bühne bieten dürfen«, resümierte Feldenkirchen, »das sehe ich ganz anders.« Lesen Sie mehr dazu hier.
description: Erfolgsautorin Juli Zeh hat erst kürzlich einen neuen Roman veröffentlicht. Da bleibt womöglich nicht mehr viel Zeit für ein Ehrenamt. Einem Bericht zufolge hat sie nun um einen entsprechenden Rücktritt gebeten.
